demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use an Accordion for content people can explore one section at a time, such as answers, settings, or a course outline. Each heading is a button that opens its panel.
demos.caption: Press “What is your return policy?”. Its answer opens and the shipping answer closes. Press the same heading again to close it.

demos.heading: Multiple
demos.intro: Add `multiple` to let several items stay open. Opening one then leaves the others as they are.
demos.caption: Open Privacy and security. Notification settings stays open; close either section independently.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Set `disabled` on an item or on a single trigger to prevent changes, or on the accordion to disable every item. Disabled triggers stay in the tab order so people can still discover them. A disabled `<fieldset>` around the accordion disables it too.
demos.caption: Tab to Premium feature information. It stays focusable, and pressing it leaves its panel closed. Try “How do I update my email address?” instead.

demos.heading: Collapsible
demos.intro: The open trigger reports `aria-disabled="true"` because pressing it leaves its panel open.
demos.caption: Open Timeline, then press it again. It stays open until you choose another heading.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: An item can refuse a change: call `details.cancel()` in its `onOpenChange` callback. Item callbacks run before the accordion's `onValueChange`, including the item that would close when another opens. Canceling any one of them cancels the whole change. `onValueChange` also gets the reason for the change.
demos.caption: Press Security to open it, then press it again. Cancel the confirmation and Security stays open; accept it and the section closes.

demos.heading: Keep Mounted
demos.intro: A closed panel normally unmounts. Add `keepMounted` to one panel or the whole accordion to keep its content hidden in the page. This preserves local state, such as a draft in a field.
demos.caption: Write a message, switch to Formatting, then return to Reply to this thread. Your draft is still there.

demos.heading: Find in Page
demos.intro: Add `hiddenUntilFound` to keep closed panels available to the browser's Find command. A match opens the item immediately, without an animation, with the reason `find-in-page`.
demos.caption: Use your browser’s Find command to search for “pineapple”. The closed “Which fruit do you stock?” panel opens to reveal the match.

demos.heading: Find in Page
demos.intro: A link to an element inside a closed panel can reveal it too. Give the target an `id` and link to it with a hash, such as `href="#refund-timeline"`.
demos.caption: Press Jump to the refund timeline. The closed Refunds panel opens and the browser moves to the linked paragraph.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: The panel stays mounted until its exit animation finishes. An item's `onOpenChangeComplete` runs afterward with the open state. A panel that starts open appears right away, with no animation and no completion callback.
demos.caption: Open or close an item. Its panel animates its height.

demos.heading: Expand All
demos.intro: With `multiple`, a controller's `openAll()` opens every enabled item. `closeAll()` closes every item that may close. Controllers explains how to connect one.
demos.caption: Press Expand all or Collapse all. Open an individual week near the bottom to scroll it into view after its panel opens.

demos.heading: Nested
demos.intro: Put another accordion inside a panel when a section has its own expandable sections. Each accordion tracks its own items. Give the inner headings a lower level than the outer headings.
demos.caption: Open Billing, then Invoices inside it. The inner accordion changes without closing Billing.

demos.heading: FAQ Search
demos.intro: Combine a search field with a controlled accordion: filter the questions and set `value` to the matching items. The example also highlights matches and leaves the triggers usable while the search is active.
demos.caption: Search for “refund” to show and open matching answers. Try “zzz” for the empty result, then clear the search to restore all questions.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Use a `render` snippet to choose another heading level or element. Parts and Composition covers custom elements and part state. Accordion's states are listed under State.
demos.caption: Each step is an h4 with its number and a Show or Hide hint that follows its open state. Open Import the parts to see it update.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use an alert dialog when someone needs to answer a question before an action continues, such as deleting a project.
demos.caption: Open the dialog with Enter to start on Cancel. Tab stays inside, clicking outside leaves it open, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Use `bind:open` when your app needs to read or control whether the dialog is open. State and Events explains controlled state and canceling a change.
demos.caption: Choose Review Changes, then Keep Editing or Discard.

demos.heading: Shortcut
demos.intro: Give the trigger a `shortcut` to open the dialog from the keyboard, and put `AlertDialogShortcut` inside it to show the keys. Dialog covers the shortcut syntax.
demos.caption: Press Cmd+Shift+H (Ctrl+Shift+H on Windows and Linux) to open the dialog without clicking.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: The content has `data-starting-style` while it opens and `data-ending-style` while it closes. Transition from those states, and the dialog stays mounted until the exit finishes:
demos.caption: Open and close the dialog. It slides up and fades in, and slides down and fades out before it unmounts.

demos.heading: Nested
demos.intro: An alert dialog opened inside another joins its stack, such as a second confirmation before something can't be undone. Escape closes the topmost one and returns focus to its trigger. The dialog underneath gets `data-nested-open`, so you can show which layer is active. To close both once the last question is answered, control the outer dialog with `bind:open` and close it when the inner one's `onOpenChange` reports `returnValue` `"confirm"`.
demos.caption: Choose Delete Workspace, then Delete. Press Escape to step back to the first question, or choose Delete Workspace to close both.

demos.heading: Async Action
demos.intro: An `action` on a Close part runs before it closes the dialog. Return a Promise to keep the dialog open until the work finishes. A resolved Promise closes it with the reason `action`; a rejection keeps it open and puts the error in that part's state.
demos.caption: Choose Delete Project, then Delete. The first attempt fails so you can try again. While Deleting… is shown, Cancel and Escape leave the dialog open. A successful retry closes it.

demos.heading: Confirm From Anywhere
demos.intro: The shared `confirm()` asks a question without any dialog markup. Render `OverlayHost` from `@ui-sdk/svelte/overlays` once near the root of your app, and it shows each question as an alert dialog. `confirm()` resolves `true` when someone agrees. Confirm Options lists what you can pass.
demos.caption: Choose Archive Project, then Archive or Cancel. The console shows the answer.

demos.heading: Confirm
demos.intro: `await confirm({ name })` resolves `true` when the Close part with `value="confirm"` closes the dialog. Cancel, Escape, and other answers resolve `false`. This lets several rows share one dialog:
demos.caption: Delete a project. Cancel or Escape keeps it; Delete removes it and focuses a neighboring row's button. Reset Projects brings the list back.

demos.heading: Queued Questions
demos.intro: Calls to the same confirm function wait their turn. You can ask two questions at once; the second appears only after the first has an answer.
demos.caption: Choose Review Two Projects. Answer the Acme question, then the Globex question. The console shows both answers once the second one is in.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use Autocomplete for a text field with helpful suggestions. Choosing one fills in the field, but any text is a valid value. Use Combobox when the value should be a selected option instead.
demos.caption: Type “man”, press Down Arrow, then Enter to fill in Mango. You can also leave text that is not in the list.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: A disabled field cannot be focused or changed and submits nothing. A read-only field stays focusable and submits its value, but does not open or accept changes. Disabled suggestions are skipped by keyboard navigation and cannot fill in the field.
demos.caption: Try the Disabled and Read-only fields. In Disabled suggestion, type “b”: arrow keys skip Banana and a press cannot choose it.

demos.heading: Clear and Trigger
demos.intro: `AutocompleteClear` empties the field and returns focus to it. `AutocompleteTrigger` lets someone open the suggestions without typing. Give the trigger a label that describes what it opens.
demos.caption: Clear Mango, then press Show fruits to open the suggestions. The clear button disappears while the field is empty.

demos.heading: Open on Focus
demos.intro: Add `openOnFocus` to offer suggestions as soon as the input receives focus. This works well when there are useful choices before someone types.
demos.caption: Focus Search docs to see recent searches before typing. Escape closes them; pressing the field opens them again.

demos.heading: Auto Highlight
demos.intro: `autoHighlight` highlights the first match while typing, so Enter can choose it immediately. Set `loop` to `false` to stop arrow keys at either end of the list.
demos.caption: Type “pe” and press Enter to choose the first match. Arrow keys stop at the ends because this example disables looping.

demos.heading: Inline Completion
demos.intro: `inlineComplete` fills in the rest of the first suggestion that starts with the typed text, with the added text selected. Arrow keys fill in the suggestion they highlight. End or Right Arrow accepts the completion; Backspace or Escape takes it back out.
demos.caption: Type “bl” to complete blackberry inline. Backspace removes the completion; Down Arrow fills in Blueberry. Press End to accept the text.

demos.heading: Highlight Matches
demos.intro: `AutocompleteItemText` marks the matching text, ignoring case and accents using the current locale. Its state exposes the matching segments when you want to render them yourself, as this example does in bold.
demos.caption: Type “berry”. The matching letters are bold while each suggestion keeps its original spelling.

demos.heading: Filter and Keywords
demos.intro: The default filter matches text anywhere in a suggestion. Use `"startsWith"` or `"fuzzy"` for a different match, a function for your own filter, or `false` for results already filtered by a server. `keywords` adds searchable text without changing what goes in the field.
demos.caption: Type “bug” to find fix through its keywords. Type “re” to find labels or keywords that start with those letters.

demos.heading: Groups
demos.intro: Use `AutocompleteGroup` and `AutocompleteGroupLabel` to name related suggestions. Filtering hides empty groups and separators.
demos.caption: Type “an”. Banana and Mango remain in Tropical; groups with no matches disappear.

demos.heading: Icons
demos.intro: `AutocompleteItemIcon` keeps decorative icons out of accessible names, filtering, and the text put in the field. Add `mirror` for directional icons. An icon-only suggestion still needs an `aria-label`.
demos.caption: Type “rep” and choose Replies. The icon stays out of the text put in the field.

demos.heading: Items as Data
demos.intro: Map an array into parts when you want to write the markup yourself. This example maps fruit groups and adds a separator between them.
demos.caption: Open the list to see three fruit groups. Type “an” to narrow them to Banana and Mango.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: The value is always a string. Control it with `value` and `onValueChange`, or start uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. Suggestions have a separate `open` state and `onOpenChange`. Callbacks receive the proposed value first, then change details. Call `details.cancel()` to reject a text or open change. State and Events covers controlled state and cancellation.
demos.caption: Type more than 12 characters and the extra text is refused. The console shows each change and its reason.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: Create a `createAutocompleteController()` for one instance and pass it as `controller`. It can `setValue()`, `clear()`, `focus()`, `setOpen()`, or read `getValue()` and `isOpen()`. `open()` returns a promise that resolves when the popup closes, including abort and unmount; `close()` closes it. See Controllers for lifecycle and change options.
demos.caption: Use the buttons to open the suggestions, type Pea, clear the field or focus it from outside.

demos.heading: Positioning
demos.intro: Use `side`, `align`, offsets, or a custom `anchor` to position the suggestions. `container` chooses where they render, and `keepMounted` keeps closed content in the DOM. Popups covers positioning, portals, animation, and modal behavior.
demos.caption: Open the suggestions. They appear above the card, aligned to its end.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: The content has `data-starting-style` while it opens and `data-ending-style` while it closes. Transition from those states, and the popup stays mounted until the exit finishes:
demos.caption: Type to open the suggestions. They slide and fade in, and fade out before they unmount.

demos.heading: Presentation
demos.intro: A sheet is modal unless `modal` is `false`. Give it a height, keep suggestions inside `AutocompleteList`, and leave the content’s `translate` alone so dragging can move it. Use `data-presentation` to style both presentations and `--sheet-backdrop` to set the dimmed background.
demos.caption: Open the field to see a sheet. On touch, tap the field in its header to show the keyboard, or swipe down to close it.

demos.heading: Forms
demos.intro: The native input is the form control: `name` gives its submitted key, `required` rejects empty text, and reset restores `defaultValue`. Text does not have to match a suggestion. Use `form` to associate the field with a form elsewhere in the page.
demos.caption: Submit Apple, then choose Mango. Choosing it fills the field without submitting. Reset restores Apple.

demos.heading: Search
demos.intro: Choosing a suggestion normally only fills in the field. Add `submitOnSelect` to search as soon as someone chooses one.
demos.caption: Type “kotlin” and press Enter to search. Choose a suggestion to search for that text instead.

demos.heading: Recent Searches
demos.intro: Pair `emptyItems` with `items` to show one collection while the field is empty and search the full collection once someone types. Add `openOnFocus` to show the recent searches on focus.
demos.caption: Focus the empty field to see Recent searches. Type “react” to search all topics, then clear the text to return to recent searches.

demos.heading: Async Suggestions
demos.intro: `AutocompleteStatus` and `AutocompleteEmpty` provide loading, error, and empty messages. Without a status part, `announcement` controls what screen readers hear when typing pauses. `onLoadMore` can request another page when scrolling or highlighting reaches the last suggestion.
demos.caption: Type “b” and wait for the city suggestions. Keep typing to replace the search; the status describes the latest results.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Use a `render` snippet to give a suggestion a different element. Here each suggestion is a link, so the autocomplete works as a jump-to menu: Enter or a click follows the highlighted link, and the text after the title is a hint that doesn't affect filtering. Parts and Composition covers the render API.
demos.caption: Type “sty” and press Enter to jump to the Styling section of this page.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use an Avatar for a person or a team, like in a comment, a member list or an account menu. It shows initials or an icon until the image loads, and keeps showing them if the image fails.
demos.caption: The image replaces the initials once it loads. A screen reader can read the person's name in either state.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Button renders a native `button` and adds what it doesn't do on its own: it stays pending while an async action runs, so a form can't submit twice, announces slow actions to screen readers, can stay focusable while disabled, and keeps the same behavior when it renders a link. For a plain click handler, a native `button` is enough.
demos.caption: Click Button, or focus it and press Enter or Space. The console logs each press.

demos.heading: Pending
demos.intro: After one second, it announces "Loading" to screen readers. Set `pendingAnnouncement` to change that message, as above, or use an empty string to silence it.
demos.caption: Press Save, then press it again while it saves. Nothing happens until the first action finishes.

demos.heading: Pending Content
demos.intro: To change what the button shows while it waits, mark content with `data-show="idle"` or `data-show="pending"` and hide it in the other state with one CSS rule each, or use Tailwind's `in-data-pending` variant:
demos.caption: Press Save. Its arrow turns into a spinner while it saves.

demos.heading: Handling Errors
demos.intro: The demo uses a `render` snippet to show the error beside the button. The `children` snippet receives the state too.
demos.caption: Choose Save Changes. Saving always fails here: the console shows the error and the label changes to Try Again.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Set `disabled` to prevent presses and remove the button from the tab order. A disabled `<fieldset>` around the button disables it too.
demos.caption: Try clicking the button. It does nothing, and Tab skips it.

demos.heading: Focusable When Disabled
demos.intro: Use `aria-describedby` to explain why the action is unavailable:
demos.caption: Focus Title, then press Tab to reach Publish while it is disabled. Enter a title to enable it, then choose Publish. The console logs what was published.

demos.heading: Links
demos.intro: Use the `render` snippet to render an `<a>`, and spread the supplied `props` onto it. It keeps its `href` and link semantics, including opening in a new tab. A disabled link cannot navigate and leaves the tab order.
demos.caption: Choose Get Started to jump to Installation on this page. Changelog is disabled and does not navigate.

demos.heading: Forms
demos.intro: Set `type="submit"` to submit a form or `type="reset"` to restore its default values. The default, `type="button"`, does neither.
demos.caption: Edit the email and choose Subscribe, or press Enter in the field. The console logs each submission, and Reset restores the original email.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Calendar shows dates directly on the page. Use it for a booking flow, a schedule, or any place where the dates should stay visible. For a text field that opens a calendar, use Date Picker.
demos.caption: Choose a date, then use Previous or Next to change the month. Arrow keys move through the days.

demos.heading: Range
demos.intro: `mode="range"` chooses a start and then an end. Moving the pointer or focus previews the range; the value changes once both ends are chosen. A date before the start ends it too, and becomes the start. Escape cancels an unfinished range.
demos.caption: Choose a start date, then move to an end date to preview the range. Choose the end to finish, or press Escape to cancel the unfinished range.

demos.heading: Multiple
demos.intro: `mode="multiple"` toggles each date independently. Its value is a sorted array, even when dates were chosen in another order.
demos.caption: Choose another date to add it, or choose a selected date to remove it.

demos.heading: Unavailable Dates
demos.intro: Unavailable dates cannot be selected, but stay focusable so keyboard and screen reader users can discover them. They expose `aria-disabled` and `data-unavailable`.
demos.caption: Try an unavailable date, then choose an available one. Unavailable days remain focusable so their state can be heard.

demos.heading: Min and Max
demos.intro: `min` and `max` set the earliest and latest selectable dates. Dates outside those bounds cannot receive focus. Arrow keys stop at the bounds, and Previous and Next stop at their months.
demos.caption: Move toward either end of the allowed dates. Keyboard navigation and month buttons stop at the limits.

demos.heading: Disabled and Read Only
demos.intro: `disabled` prevents focus, selection, and month navigation. `readOnly` allows navigation so dates can be inspected, but keeps the selected value unchanged.
demos.caption: Try choosing a date or changing months. A disabled calendar has no available controls.

demos.heading: Disabled and Read Only
demos.intro: `disabled` prevents focus, selection, and month navigation. `readOnly` allows navigation so dates can be inspected, but keeps the selected value unchanged.
demos.caption: Move through dates and months. The selected value stays unchanged.

demos.heading: Two Months
demos.intro: `pageBy="page"` makes Previous, Next, and navigation beyond the visible grids move by the full number of months.
demos.caption: Move between October and November with arrow keys. Next advances both visible months to December and January.

demos.heading: Fixed Weeks
demos.intro: `fixedWeeks` renders six week rows in every month. Set `showOutsideDays` to `false` to leave dates from neighboring months blank.
demos.caption: Move from February to March. Both grids keep six week rows, and dates outside each month are hidden.

demos.heading: Month and Year Selects
demos.intro: They update the first displayed month with the `select-change` reason. Their state exposes the options if you want to render a different select.
demos.caption: Choose a year and month to jump directly to a birthday, then choose the day.

demos.heading: Custom Month and Year Selects
demos.intro: The month and year selects are native `select` elements. To use your own select, control the calendar's `month` and drive it from your select's value, as with the Select component here. Keep a `CalendarHeading` in the calendar, visually hidden if you like, so the grid stays named.
demos.caption: Choose a month or a year from the selects. The calendar follows, and the arrow keys still move between days.

demos.heading: Language
demos.intro: Previous and Next are named "Previous month" and "Next month". Pass `aria-label` to name them in another language. Dates remain Gregorian. Localized year systems, such as Buddhist or Japanese era years, can still appear in the labels.
demos.caption: Move through the calendar. Month names, weekday headers, and full date labels are in German, with Monday first.

demos.heading: Name Formats
demos.intro: Set `weekdayFormat` for the weekday headers and `monthFormat` for the heading and the month select. Both take `"narrow"`, `"short"` or `"long"`, and follow the calendar's locale. Screen readers still hear full names: the grid and each day keep their long labels.
demos.caption: The weekday headers are narrow and the heading uses short month names: Oct – Nov 2026.

demos.heading: Custom Days
demos.intro: A day’s `children` snippet receives its state, including the date, label, selection, and whether it is outside the month. This example adds a price below each day. Weekday headers can have custom content too.
demos.caption: Choose a date to see its price selected with it. Dates outside the current month have no price.

demos.heading: Range Limits
demos.intro: A range cannot include an unavailable date unless `allowUnavailable` is set. That allows unavailable dates between the ends; they still cannot be chosen as an endpoint.
demos.caption: In October 2026, choose October 15 then October 20. This example accepts 3–8 days and allows the range to span the unavailable weekend.

demos.heading: Range in Progress
demos.intro: The root's state has `anchor`, the start while an end is being picked, and `focused`, the date with the Tab stop. `onAnchorChange` and `onFocusedChange` report them before they change, to show the range being picked outside the calendar, and canceling either keeps things as they were. A day that takes focus because the months turned reports nothing.
demos.caption: Choose a start date, then move with the arrow keys. The console logs the start and each focused date until Enter picks the end.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Use `value` with `onValueChange` and `month` with `onMonthChange` to control them. Use `defaultValue` and `defaultMonth` for initial state. Change details include a reason; `details.cancel()` rejects the change. State and Events covers the binding pattern, and the reason tables list Calendar’s reasons.
demos.caption: Choose a date or change the month. The console logs each change and its reason.

demos.heading: Today
demos.intro: `timeZone` determines which date is today. It does not convert the selected date into another time zone.
demos.caption: Find the marked date for today in Pacific/Kiritimati, which may differ from today in your time zone.

demos.heading: Driving It from Anywhere
demos.intro: A `createCalendarController()` instance can set the value, change months, and focus a date. Focusing a date in another month shows that month first. Controllers covers setup and lifecycle.
demos.caption: Press Go to Christmas to select December 25 and move focus there, or Today to jump back to today and select it.

demos.heading: Presets
demos.intro: Drive a range calendar from buttons for the ranges people pick most. Each preset sets the value through the controller and moves focus to its first day, using the date helpers for the arithmetic.
demos.caption: Choose Last 7 Days, This Month or Next 30 Days. The range is selected and the calendar shows its start.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: The grid’s `children` snippet receives its state, with its month, label, weekdays, and weeks, when you need to write the table yourself. Preserve empty cells marked `hidden` so dates shown by another month do not appear twice. Parts and Composition covers changing a part’s element without losing its behavior.
demos.caption: The table is your own markup, built from the grid's state. Navigate and select as usual.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Carousel to show a set of slides one view at a time, like product photos or featured stories. It scrolls natively, so swipes and trackpads work, and Previous and Next buttons page through the slides.
demos.caption: Use Previous and Next, swipe the slides, or focus the viewport and use the arrow keys.

demos.heading: Vertical
demos.intro: `orientation="vertical"` scrolls up and down. Give the viewport a height. Up and down arrows page it, not left and right.
demos.caption: Scroll vertically, or use the up and down controls.

demos.heading: Loop
demos.intro: The slides take turns at the ends of the content with CSS `order` while the carousel rests, so the current page always has slides on both sides. They keep their place in the document, so screen readers and Tab follow the slides' own order. The content needs to lay its slides out in a row with even gaps, as flex and grid do, and hold a page of slides to either side of the current one. With fewer, like two slides one to a view, Next on the last page scrolls back to the first instead.
demos.caption: Keep moving forward or backward to wrap around the slides.

demos.heading: Align
demos.intro: `align` lines pages up at the viewport's `start` (the default), `center` or `end`. Centered slides narrower than the viewport let their neighbors peek in. The first and last pages stay at the ends of the content, so there's no empty space before the first slide.
demos.caption: Choose Start, Center or End, then page through the slides. Centered slides let their neighbors peek in on both sides.

demos.heading: Default Page
demos.intro: `defaultPage` is the page it starts on, when uncontrolled. It's 1 by default.
demos.caption: Start on the chosen page, then move forward or backward.

demos.heading: Indicators
demos.intro: Write one per slide. Those past the page count hide themselves, so the same markup works however many slides fit. An indicator's `page` is inferred from their order; pass it to render the selected one on the server.
demos.caption: Choose a named indicator, then use arrows, Home, and End to move between them.

demos.heading: Pages
demos.intro: `slidesPerPage` is how many slides a page holds: Next moves that many, and each indicator stands for that many. `"auto"` fits as many as show. Pages that can't reach the start, like the last few slides, merge into the last page. With three slides in view, five slides make three pages at one slide per page, or two pages at three per page.
demos.caption: Move through groups of slides using the page controls.

demos.heading: Thumbnails
demos.intro: A gallery and a strip of thumbnails share the selected page. The thumbnail carousel scrolls freely with `dragFree` and fits as many as show. Pressing a thumbnail selects its slide.
demos.caption: Choose a thumbnail to change the gallery, or scroll either strip.

demos.heading: Autoplay
demos.intro: `--carousel-interval` on the root is the interval, and `data-paused` is there while it's paused, so a progress bar can time itself with CSS.
demos.caption: Start or stop rotation. Hover to pause it, or move keyboard focus inside to stop it. The console logs each change and why.

demos.heading: Progress
demos.intro: `onPageChangeComplete` runs once the slides come to rest on a page, after a spring, a drag or a scroll. Start work there that would stutter the motion, like loading the next slides' images.
demos.caption: Move through the slides. The progress bar follows the scroll position, and the console logs the slide it rests on.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Every change carries a reason: `next-press` and `previous-press` for the parts, `item-press` for an indicator, `list-navigation` for arrow keys, `swipe` for a finger or a mouse drag, `scroll` for a wheel or trackpad, `timeout` for rotation and `imperative` from a controller. Call `details.cancel()` to stay on the page: a swipe or drag springs back. A controlled page that doesn't change scrolls back too.
demos.caption: Change the page. The console logs each page and the reason for the change.

demos.heading: Paging from Anywhere
demos.intro: `drag={false}` turns off swiping and dragging, so only the parts, keys and controllers move it.
demos.caption: Use the controls outside the carousel to change its page.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Every part takes a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state, and the `children` snippet receives the state too: a slide's `index`, `active` and `inView`, a step's `disabled`, an indicator's `page` and `selected`, the play toggle's `playing` and `paused`.
demos.caption: Change slides to see each slide and control describe its current state.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a checkbox for a choice someone can check or uncheck. Use a group when several choices belong to one value.
demos.caption: Click the checkbox or its label, or focus it and press Space, to accept the terms.

demos.heading: Description
demos.intro: Use `FieldLabel` and `FieldDescription` when a choice needs more explanation. The field connects both to the checkbox.
demos.caption: Click Accept terms and conditions. The field connects the label and description to the checkbox.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: `disabled` prevents focus and changes, and leaves the checkbox out of form submissions. A disabled `fieldset` does the same.
demos.caption: Security alerts are always on, so that checkbox is disabled. Clicking its label leaves it checked.

demos.heading: Read-Only
demos.intro: `readOnly` keeps the checkbox focusable and included in form submissions, while preventing the user from changing it.
demos.caption: Tab to the checked checkbox. Space and clicks leave the setting unchanged.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Use `bind:checked` to own the value. A controller from `createCheckboxController()` changes it from anywhere, like the Toggle button below.
demos.caption: Change the checkbox, or press Toggle. The console logs each change and its reason.

demos.heading: Forms
demos.intro: `required` blocks submission until the checkbox is checked. Reset returns it to `defaultChecked`. Set `form` to a form's id to join it from elsewhere on the page.
demos.caption: Create the account with the terms unchecked to see native validation, then accept them and try again. The console logs what was submitted, and Reset restores the defaults.

demos.heading: Group
demos.intro: `CheckboxGroup` keeps one list of checked values. Each checkbox supplies its `value`; the group returns selected values in the order the checkboxes appear. Name the group with `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or a Field.
demos.caption: Choose several toppings. The group keeps one list of checked values.

demos.heading: Parent Checkbox
demos.intro: Pass `allValues` to the group so the parent has the right state on the first render, including on the server. Otherwise it discovers the values after the checkboxes mount.
demos.caption: Select all checks every topping. Uncheck one topping to put Select all into its mixed state.

demos.heading: Disabled Group
demos.intro: Disable the group to lock every checkbox, or disable one child to keep just that value fixed. A parent changes only enabled children.
demos.caption: The Backups group is disabled. In Sync folders, Select all changes the enabled folders while Desktop stays checked.

demos.heading: Controlled Group
demos.intro: Use `bind:value` to own the selected values. A controller can replace that list, as Select Weekdays and Clear do below.
demos.caption: Choose working days, or press Select Weekdays or Clear. The console logs the group's value and the reason it changed.

demos.heading: Group in a Form
demos.intro: In a field, the field supplies the group's label and description, and `FieldError` shows the validation message inline until a selection makes the group valid. Forms and Validation covers the shared field behavior.
demos.caption: Save with nothing checked to see the inline error. Choose a notification method and save; the console logs the submitted values.

demos.heading: Table
demos.intro: The same parent checkbox can select rows from a table header. Each row supplies its value and accessible name.
demos.caption: Select rows individually, or use Select all in the header. The console logs how many are selected.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: `keepMounted` keeps the indicator in the page while unchecked, with `data-unchecked`, for styles that show both states.
demos.caption: Check and uncheck a task. The check scales and fades in, and out before it unmounts.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: The checkbox, indicator, and group take a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state. Keep the part's props on the interactive element so its role, label, and keyboard behavior stay connected.
demos.caption: Choose topics. Each checkbox renders a button that shows a check or a plus from its state.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a collapsible to show and hide one panel of content. For a set of panels, use an accordion.
demos.caption: Press Order #4189, or focus it and press Enter or Space, to show the items.

demos.heading: Keep Mounted
demos.intro: Panels unmount when they close, so Tab skips their contents. Set `keepMounted` on the panel to keep it mounted and hidden, so a field keeps what you typed into it.
demos.caption: Open Add a delivery note, type a note, then close and reopen the panel. Your note is still there.

demos.heading: Find in Page
demos.intro: Svelte renders `hidden="until-found"` on the server, so the closed panel is findable before hydration.
demos.caption: Leave Ingredients closed. Open your browser's Find command and search for cardamom to reveal the panel.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: For a button elsewhere on the page, create a controller with `createCollapsibleController()` and pass it as `controller`. Create one controller per mounted collapsible.
demos.caption: Open Recovery codes with Toggle or its trigger, then press Done. The console logs each change and its reason, and Done returns focus to the trigger.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: `onOpenChangeComplete` reports when opening or closing has finished.
demos.caption: Open and close Release notes. The console logs when each animation finishes.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Use a part's `render` snippet to choose its element, and read its state from that snippet or from `children`. The trigger below renders inside a heading, and the panel renders as an ordered list.
demos.caption: Press Track parcel to open the ordered list. The summary changes from Arrives Thursday to 3 updates.

demos.heading: OKLCH
demos.intro: OKLCH spaces its colors evenly for the eye, so two colors with the same lightness look equally bright. Its edge with the colors a screen can show is a curve, which no gradient can draw. Add `ColorPickerAreaCanvas` to the area, and it paints the colors inside that edge and leaves the rest clear.
demos.caption: Drag the thumb right, past the painted edge, and let go. The thumb moves back to the closest color inside.

demos.heading: Presets and Channel Inputs
demos.intro: `ColorPickerChannelInput` edits one channel as a number and sets it on Enter, when you leave it, or with its arrows. `ColorPickerEyeDropper` picks from the screen in browsers that can. Elsewhere it's disabled, with `data-unsupported`, so you can hide it.
demos.caption: Choose a preset, or use the arrow keys between them. Type 255 into the first number to set red.

demos.heading: Popover
demos.intro: Put a `Popover` inside the picker to open it from a swatch. The parts inside the popup edit the same color, and the swatch in the trigger shows it.
demos.caption: Press the Background swatch to open the picker, then drag to change the color.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Set `disabled`. A disabled picker can't be focused or changed, and isn't submitted. A disabled `<fieldset>` around it disables it too.
demos.caption: The thumbs can't be focused or dragged.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: `onValueChange` runs on every step of a drag. `onValueCommit` runs once, when the drag, key press or typed color ends, so use it to save. A controller from `createColorPickerController()` sets the color from anywhere with `setValue()`, like the Use Purple button below.
demos.caption: Drag across the area and let go, or press Use Purple. The console logs each committed color and its reason.

demos.heading: Form
demos.intro: The hidden input submits the value under `name`, like `#f97316`, and a disabled picker submits nothing. A form reset returns it to `defaultValue`. Set `form` to join a form by its id.
demos.caption: Change the color and press Save to log the submitted value. Reset restores the orange.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Combobox when people need to find a choice by typing. Start with an input and a list, then add chips, server results, or the option to create something new as you need them.
demos.caption: Type “sv” to find SvelteKit. Press Down Arrow to highlight it, then Enter to choose it.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: A disabled combobox cannot be focused or changed and submits nothing. A read-only one remains focusable and submits its value, but does not open or accept changes. Keyboard navigation skips a disabled option, and it cannot be chosen.
demos.caption: Billing country is disabled and Shipping from is read-only. Open Shipping to: arrow keys skip Denmark, which can't be chosen.

demos.heading: Clear and Trigger
demos.intro: `ComboboxClear` clears both the selection and the query, then keeps focus in the input. It appears while either has a value. When someone deletes all the text, a single selection clears right away instead of when the list closes. Escape brings the selection back while the list is still open; closing it any other way leaves it cleared.
demos.caption: Choose a framework, then press the clear button. The selection and text clear, focus stays in the input, and the console logs each change.

demos.heading: Auto Highlight
demos.intro: Add `autoHighlight` to highlight the first match while typing, so Enter can choose it immediately. With `autoHighlight="always"`, opening the list also highlights the selected item, or the first, so the arrow keys move from there. A highlight it placed follows the list as items arrive, and one the user moved stays while its item is there.
demos.caption: Type “sw” and press Enter. The first matching country is already highlighted.

demos.heading: Highlight Matches
demos.intro: `ComboboxItemText` marks the matching text. Matching ignores case and accents using the current locale, while the label keeps its original spelling. Its state also exposes segments if you want to render the marks yourself.
demos.caption: Type “an”. Matching letters are marked while each country keeps its original spelling.

demos.heading: Filter and Keywords
demos.intro: Use `keywords` for text that should match without appearing in the label, such as a username or a country’s local name.
demos.caption: Type “an” and switch Filter between Contains and Starts with. Choose Fuzzy and type “swd” for Sweden, or type “deutschland” to find Germany through a keyword.

demos.heading: Groups
demos.intro: Use `ComboboxGroup` and `ComboboxGroupLabel` to name groups. Filtering hides empty groups and separators as their items disappear.
demos.caption: Type “chic”. Chicago remains in Americas; groups with no matches disappear.

demos.heading: Icons
demos.intro: Wrap the input and icon together, then use that wrapper as the popup’s `anchor`. Add `mirror` for directional icons. An icon-only option still needs an `aria-label`.
demos.caption: Choose Done. Its icon appears next to the input as well as in the list.

demos.heading: Custom Items
demos.intro: Show useful context beside a label, such as a username or role. Set `label` explicitly so filtering and the input use the intended text, and put extra search terms in `keywords`.
demos.caption: Search for a person’s name or username. Choose a result to put that person’s name in the input.

demos.heading: Recent Items
demos.intro: `emptyItems` supplies suggestions while the query is empty. Pair it with `items` for the full searchable collection. Render the list from `state.items` so it follows the active collection.
demos.caption: Open the empty input to see Recent. Start typing to search all countries; clear the text to return to Recent.

demos.heading: Multiple
demos.intro: Add `keepQuery` to choose several matches without retyping the query.
demos.caption: Choose several frameworks. Remove one with its chip button, or press Backspace in the empty input to remove the last chip.

demos.heading: Select All
demos.intro: `ComboboxSelectAll` toggles every matching, enabled option. Inside a group, it affects only that group. It joins keyboard navigation and reports a mixed state while some of its options are selected.
demos.caption: Open the list and choose a group’s select-all option. Type to narrow the matches, then use the main select-all option on those results.

demos.heading: Chips That Collapse
demos.intro: Add `ComboboxChipsOverflow` to keep chips on one line. It measures which chips fit, hides the rest, and exposes their count and labels. Separately, `ComboboxValue` can use `max` to show a short text summary of the selection.
demos.caption: Add or remove countries. Chips that no longer fit are replaced by an overflow count; the summary below lists the first two.

demos.heading: Max Selected
demos.intro: `maxSelected` limits a multiple selection. Once the limit is reached, other options become disabled; their `maxReached` state explains why.
demos.caption: Choose a third label. Other unselected labels become unavailable until you remove one.

demos.heading: Create Option
demos.intro: While saving, the option reports `data-pending`, `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`. A rejected promise is available through its error state.
demos.caption: Type a new label and choose Create. It becomes a selected chip after saving; a label longer than 20 characters shows an error.

demos.heading: Custom Value
demos.intro: Use `allowCustomValue` when suggestions are optional, like a datalist. Unmatched text becomes the value on Enter with nothing highlighted, or when the list closes. This does not create a new item in the collection.
demos.caption: Type a job title that isn't suggested, then press Enter without a highlighted option or leave the field. The text becomes the value, and the console logs it.

demos.heading: Input in the Popup
demos.intro: The input can live inside the popup, opened by a button showing the current value. The button then stays in the tab order. Anchor the content to it, clear the query when opening, and return focus to it after closing, as this example does.
demos.caption: Press Country to open the search field inside the popup. Choose a country; closing the popup returns focus to the button.

demos.heading: Async Search
demos.intro: `ComboboxStatus` and `ComboboxEmpty` provide loading, error, and empty messages. Without a custom status, the combobox announces the result count once typing pauses.
demos.caption: Replace “the” with another movie title. The status shows the pending search, then the latest results.

demos.heading: Load More
demos.intro: `onLoadMore` runs when scrolling or highlighting reaches the last option, once per page and not while a page loads. Connect it to the async loader’s `loadMore()`; return `{ items, hasMore }` from each page.
demos.caption: Open the movies and scroll or arrow to the last result. Another page loads while the existing results stay available.

demos.heading: Virtualized
demos.intro: This example windows 10,000 items. Keep the actual row height aligned with your virtualizer’s measurement, and use the scroller’s visible height when revealing a row.
demos.caption: Search 10,000 items or move through them with the arrow keys. Only the nearby rows render.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Focus leaving the input closes the popup with the reason `focus-out`, even when code moves it, like a notice that takes focus. To keep the popup open, cancel that close in `onOpenChange`.
demos.caption: Type, choose, or use the buttons. The console logs each value, query and open change with its reason.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: Pass a controller from `createComboboxController()`. It can read or set the value and query, open or close the list, and focus the input. `open()` resolves when the list closes with its reason and source, including `unmount`; pass an abort signal to close it on cancellation. Controllers covers lifetime and setup.
demos.caption: Use the buttons to drive the combobox from outside. Open and Wait logs how the list closed and what was chosen.

demos.heading: Positioning
demos.intro: The page stays usable by default. `modal="pointer"` makes an outside press only dismiss the list; `modal` also locks scrolling and makes the rest of the page inert. The popup uses the top layer and renders in place; use `container` when its DOM belongs elsewhere, such as a shadow root.
demos.caption: Pick a side and an alignment, then open the list. Check Anchor to the Box to place it against the box instead of the input.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: The content has `data-starting-style` while it opens and `data-ending-style` while it closes. Transition from those states, and the popup stays mounted until the exit finishes. `onOpenChangeComplete` runs after opening or closing finishes, and `keepMounted` on an item indicator keeps it in the page for a selection animation.
demos.caption: Open and close the list. The console logs when each animation finishes.

demos.heading: Presentation
demos.intro: Keep the options inside `ComboboxList` so the header stays outside the listbox. Give sheet content a height, style it with `data-presentation`, and leave its `translate` for the sheet behavior. `--sheet-backdrop` controls the backdrop. The sheet is modal unless you set `modal` to false; mouse and keyboard openings keep input focus as it moves.
demos.caption: Open the field to see a sheet. On touch, tap the search field in its header to bring up the keyboard, or swipe down to close it.

demos.heading: Forms
demos.intro: In a Field, the field supplies the input's accessible name, description and error. Submitting a required field without a selection sets `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid`.
demos.caption: Submit without a country to see the inline error. Choose one and submit; the console logs the values, and Reset restores the defaults.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Every part takes a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state, and the `children` snippet receives the state too. Each part's state is listed below.
demos.caption: Open the list and move through it. The chevron flips while it's open, the highlighted person shows Enter, and the chosen one shows a check.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Command puts a search field over a list of actions. The list stays open while someone searches. You can use it on its own, or put it in a dialog to build a command palette.
demos.caption: Type “bil” to find Billing. Arrow keys move the highlight; Escape clears the search.

demos.heading: Dialog
demos.intro: Put Command inside a Dialog for a command palette. Give the dialog a title, put `shortcut="mod+k"` on its trigger, and close it when a command runs. The dialog handles dismissal and returns focus to the trigger.
demos.caption: Press Search or use Cmd+K / Ctrl+K. Choose a command to run it and close the palette; the console logs what ran.

demos.heading: Shortcuts
demos.intro: An item’s `shortcut` can run it while the command list is mounted, even when the search or current page hides it. `CommandShortcut` displays the keys for the current platform, and the item gets `aria-keyshortcuts`. Shortcuts inside a dialog run while it is open.
demos.caption: Press Cmd+P / Ctrl+P to run Profile, even when the search hides it. The console logs each command that runs.

demos.heading: Highlight Matches
demos.intro: `CommandItemText` marks the matched text. The default fuzzy filter can match letters that are apart, so one command may have several marked segments.
demos.caption: Type “prf” to find Profile. Matching letters are marked even when they are not next to each other.

demos.heading: Filter and Keywords
demos.intro: `keywords` adds search terms without changing the command's label. Use it for synonyms or names someone might type instead.
demos.caption: Type “nf” with Fuzzy to find New file. Choose Words and type “zo in” for Zoom in, or type “smiley” to find Search emoji through a keyword.

demos.heading: Pages
demos.intro: Backspace in an empty search goes back and restores the previous page’s query. Escape clears the query first, then goes back. A Go back command can call `pop()` on a controller.
demos.caption: Choose Change theme or Switch team. Use Go back, or press Backspace in an empty search field, to return.

demos.heading: Items as Data
demos.intro: Pass `emptyItems` alongside `items` to show suggested or recent commands while the first page's search is empty. Once someone types, the full collection is searched.
demos.caption: Choose Change theme to open its commands. Press Cmd+I / Ctrl+I to run Open inbox from any page; the console logs what ran.

demos.heading: Async Results
demos.intro: `CommandStatus` describes loading and failures, and the list gets `aria-busy` while loading. `onLoadMore` can request another page when scrolling or highlighting reaches the last command. Without a status part, `announcement` controls the result-count message after typing pauses.
demos.caption: Type “login” and wait for matching issues. Replace the text to start a new search; only the latest results appear.

demos.heading: Pending Actions
demos.intro: An item’s `onSelect` runs before `onAction`. Call `preventDefault()` on its event to stop the action.
demos.caption: Run Deploy to production and try it again while it's pending. Sync with server fails and can be retried; the console logs each outcome.

demos.heading: Virtualized
demos.intro: Pass the full `items` collection so filtering and keyboard navigation include commands that are not mounted. Render only visible rows, giving each its index in the current results. `onValueChange` includes that index so you can scroll a newly highlighted row into view.
demos.caption: Search 10,000 commands or move through them with the arrow keys. Only the rows near the viewport render.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind them with `bind:value`, `bind:query` and `bind:pages`, or use `defaultValue`, `defaultQuery`, and `defaultPages` for starting state. Change callbacks receive details; call `details.cancel()` to reject a change. `value` is the highlighted command, not a chosen one, and it changes as the highlight moves. `onAction` reports activation, so moving the highlight alone does not run a command. State and Events covers the shared binding pattern.
demos.caption: Open Change theme, search and move the highlight. The console logs each highlight, query and page change with its reason.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: Create a `createCommandController()` for one instance and pass it as `controller`. It can read and set the highlight, query, and page stack. Use `push()` and `pop()` to navigate pages, `run()` to run the highlighted command or a named one, and `focus()` to focus the search. See Controllers for setup and lifecycle.
demos.caption: Use the buttons to open pages, search, move the highlight and run it from outside. The console logs each command that runs.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Render a command as an anchor when it should navigate. Enter follows the highlighted link; modified clicks keep their usual browser behavior.
demos.caption: Search for Installation and press Enter. The command follows the link to that section on this page.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Date Input for dates people know by heart, like a birthday or a booking date. Each part of the date is its own small input, ordered the way the locale writes it.
demos.caption: Click the month and type 11042026. Each part moves to the next as it fills. Press ArrowUp or ArrowDown on a part to step it.

demos.heading: Field
demos.intro: The Field's label names the group, and clicking it focuses the first segment. Its description is read with the input.
demos.caption: Click Birthday to focus the month, then type a date. Screen readers read the description with the input.

demos.heading: Date and Time
demos.intro: Set `granularity` to `"hour"`, `"minute"` or `"second"` to add the time. The value becomes a local date and time like `"2026-11-02T14:30"`. For a time alone, use Time Input.
demos.caption: Tab through the date and time. Type a P or an A in the last segment to switch between AM and PM.

demos.heading: Min and Max
demos.intro: `min` and `max` take ISO dates. A date outside them is invalid: the input sets `data-invalid`, and its form won't submit.
demos.caption: Change the year of Check-in to 2027 to see it turn invalid, then back to 2026.

demos.heading: Unavailable Dates
demos.intro: `unavailable` takes the same matchers as Calendar: ISO dates, `{ from, to }` ranges, weekdays like `{ weekday: [0, 6] }`, or a function. An unavailable date is invalid with the message "This date isn't available."
demos.caption: Step the day of Delivery date back from Monday the 2nd to Sunday the 1st. The input turns invalid until you pick a weekday again.

demos.heading: Locale
demos.intro: The input reads its order, separators and clock from `locale`, or from the page's language when you leave it out. The digits are always 0 to 9, and the calendar is always the Gregorian one, so the value means the same date everywhere. On the server, the input renders in English until it reads the page's language; set `locale` when that first render matters.
demos.caption: The same date in British English, German and Japanese. Each orders its parts its own way.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Set `disabled` on the input, or on its Field or fieldset, to keep it from focus and from its form.
demos.caption: Click Start date or press Tab to reach it. Focus skips it, and the date stays November 2, 2026.

demos.heading: Read-Only
demos.intro: Set `readOnly` for a date people can focus, read and submit as it is.
demos.caption: Focus Signed on and press ArrowUp or type a digit. The date stays the same.

demos.heading: Form
demos.intro: A hidden input submits the ISO date under `name`. An empty or partly typed date submits an empty string. Set `required` to need a date before the form submits. Enter in a segment submits the form with what was typed.
demos.caption: Clear the day of Date with Backspace and choose Book to see the form stop. Fill it in and choose Book: the console logs the values. Reset brings back the defaults.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Use `bind:value` to bind the value, and `onValueChange` to get the change details too. Both get each whole date, and `null` once any part of it is erased. A half-typed date already reads `null`, so setting the value to `null` leaves it as typed. Call `clear()` on a controller to empty every segment.
demos.caption: Change Due date: the console logs each whole date. Clear sets the value to null.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: Create a controller with `createDateInputController()` and pass it as `controller` to set, clear or focus the input from elsewhere. `focus("year")` focuses a segment by its unit.
demos.caption: Choose Christmas to set the date, Edit Year to focus the year, or Clear to empty it.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Pass a `children` snippet to render the segments yourself. It gets the input's state, whose `segments` list each segment in order, with the text between them. Render a `DateInputSegment` for each in a keyed `{#each}`, and give the text between segments content of your own.
demos.caption: The segments here are separated by dashes in place of the locale's slashes. The order stays the locale's.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Date Picker combines a text field with Calendar. People can type a date in their language or choose it from the popup. Your application receives an ISO date string either way.
demos.caption: Type a date and press Enter, or open the calendar and choose a day. The field formats the date when you commit it.

demos.heading: Typing a Date
demos.intro: The field formats a valid date after it is committed, leaving your typing alone until then. Invalid text stays visible and sets `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid`; the previous value stays unchanged. Until the text is a date again, or empty, the input reports "Enter a valid date." as its validation message, so its form won't submit. The hint’s state includes an example date you can show alongside the field.
demos.caption: Type not a date and press Enter to mark the field invalid. Replace it with 10/18/2026 to clear the invalid state.

demos.heading: Range
demos.intro: For two months side by side, set `months={2}` and add a second `CalendarGrid` with `offset={1}`. `pageBy="page"` moves both months together.
demos.caption: Choose October 20, then October 23. The calendar stays open after the first date and closes after the second.

demos.heading: Presets
demos.intro: `DatePickerPreset` chooses its `value` and closes the popup. It exposes `aria-pressed` and `data-selected` when that value matches the selection. Your application calculates relative dates, such as the last seven days.
demos.caption: Open the calendar and choose Last 7 Days. Reopen it to see the selected preset.

demos.heading: Min, Max and Unavailable Dates
demos.intro: For ranges, `minDays` and `maxDays` count both endpoints. `allowUnavailable` permits unavailable dates between them, but never as an endpoint. See Range Limits.
demos.caption: Try typing 11/21/2026, past the last allowed date, then 10/17/2026, a Saturday. Both are invalid and can't be picked; 10/19/2026 is accepted.

demos.heading: Language
demos.intro: Calendar’s `weekStartsOn`, `weekdayFormat`, `fixedWeeks`, `showOutsideDays`, and `timeZone` options apply here too. Calendar shows these options without the popup.
demos.caption: Enter 3.12.2026 and press Enter. The field, format hint, and calendar use German dates.

demos.heading: Clear
demos.intro: `DatePickerClear` clears the value and focuses the input. It gets `data-empty` when there is nothing to clear. Emptying a single-date input clears its value too.
demos.caption: Press Clear to empty the value and focus the input. The Clear button disappears until there is a value again.

demos.heading: Keep It Open Until Both Dates Are Picked
demos.intro: Set `dismissible` to `false` while a choice is incomplete. Escape, an outside press, or the system back gesture then leave the popup open. `onDismissAttempt` reports intentional attempts, so you can explain what is missing. Focus leaving is refused quietly. The trigger and imperative controls can still close it.
demos.caption: Choose a check-in date, then press outside the calendar. The message asks for a check-out date before the popup can be dismissed.

demos.heading: Popup and Presentation
demos.intro: `presentation="auto"` uses a sheet on small touch screens and a popover elsewhere. `presentation="sheet"` always uses a sheet. Style the two layouts using `data-presentation`.
demos.caption: Open the calendar. On a small touch screen it opens as a sheet, and the console logs each open, close and month change.

demos.heading: Forms
demos.intro: In a Field, the field connects the label, description, and errors to the input, and shows an error for an empty required date or text that isn't a date. Its `name` is used when the picker has none, and a disabled field disables the picker.
demos.caption: Press Submit with an empty field to see the inline error, then choose a date and submit. The console logs the ISO date.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Use `value` with `onValueChange`, `month` with `onMonthChange`, and `open` with `onOpenChange` to control them. `defaultValue`, `defaultMonth`, and `defaultOpen` set initial state instead. Change details carry a reason; `details.cancel()` rejects the requested change. State and Events covers the binding pattern, and the reason tables list Date Picker’s reasons.
demos.caption: Type or choose a date. The console logs each value and the reason for the change.

demos.heading: Driving It from Anywhere
demos.intro: A `createDatePickerController()` instance can set the value, show a month, open or close the popup, and focus a date in the open calendar. Controllers covers setup and lifecycle; the controller reference lists the methods.
demos.caption: Press Choose Christmas to set the date from outside, or Open to open the calendar.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A dialog gives a task its own space: share a link, edit a record, or collect a few details. It manages focus, Escape, outside presses, and returning to where you started.
demos.caption: Open Share, then close it with either Close button, Escape, or a press outside. Focus returns to Share.

demos.heading: Scrollable Content
demos.intro: Keep the header and actions outside the scrolling area. A viewport height limit, a shrinking middle grid row, and `overflow-y: auto` keep long content usable. `initialFocus="content"` focuses the dialog itself so reading starts at the top.
demos.caption: Open Scrollable Content in a short window. Scroll the terms while the title and Decline/Accept buttons stay in view.

demos.heading: Forms
demos.intro: A form with `method="dialog"` closes the dialog on a valid submission. The submit button’s `value` becomes the `returnValue`, just like a Close part’s `value`. An ordinary form stays open until you close the dialog yourself.
demos.caption: Open New Article and choose Save Draft or Publish. The console logs the submitted button's value. An empty title prevents submission.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Use `bind:open` to keep the dialog's state in your component. Cancel a proposed change with `details.cancel()` in `onOpenChange`. `onOpenChangeComplete` reports when opening or closing has finished; see state and events for the common change contract.
demos.caption: Check Open or press Notification Settings, then close the dialog. The console logs each change, its reason and when it finishes.

demos.heading: Keyboard Shortcut
demos.intro: A trigger’s `shortcut` opens it from the keyboard. `mod+j` means Command+J on Apple platforms and Control+J elsewhere. The Shortcut part displays the right keys and the trigger exposes `aria-keyshortcuts`.
demos.caption: Press Command+J or Control+J to open New contact. The button shows the keys, and Escape returns focus to it.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: The content and backdrop have `data-starting-style` while they open and `data-ending-style` while they close. Transition from those states, and the dialog stays mounted until the exit finishes. `onOpenChangeComplete` runs after the transition, and `keepMounted` keeps the content in the page while closed.
demos.caption: Open the dialog and close it. The console logs when each animation finishes; focus returns as closing starts.

demos.heading: Modal
demos.intro: Dialogs render where you put them and use the browser's top layer. Set `container` when their DOM needs to live elsewhere, like a shadow root. The popup guide covers containers and iframes.
demos.caption: Choose a mode, open Notes, and try Tab or clicking the page. Check Close on outside press to compare dismissal.

demos.heading: Warn Before Closing a Dirty Form
demos.intro: Set `dismissible` to false while there are unsaved changes. Escape, an outside press, or a back gesture then keeps the dialog open and reports `onDismissAttempt`. Explicit Close parts and controller calls still work, so you can offer a deliberate way out.
demos.caption: Type a post, then press Escape or click outside. Keep editing returns to the field; Discard closes the dialog and clears the draft.

demos.heading: Nested Dialogs
demos.intro: A dialog opened inside another joins its stack. Escape closes the topmost dialog and returns focus to its trigger. Closing the parent also closes its children. `data-nested-open` and `--dialog-stack` let you show which layer is active.
demos.caption: Open Account, then Change Password. Press Escape once to return to Account, and again to close it.

demos.heading: Opening from a Menu Item
demos.intro: Render the dialog outside the menu and open it with the dialog’s controller. When the item disappears, the menu’s trigger becomes the place to return focus.
demos.caption: Open File Actions and choose Rename. Close the dialog to return focus to the File Actions button.

demos.heading: Opening from Anywhere
demos.intro: Connect several triggers to one `createDialogController<Payload, Result>()`. Each trigger passes a `payload`; the content's `children` snippet reads it from `state.payload`, typed with `DialogContentState<Payload>`. `controller.open({ payload })` opens it from code and returns a promise that resolves when it closes, with the reason and any `returnValue`. Each trigger remains the return-focus target for the dialog it opened. See controllers for the shared controller pattern.
demos.caption: Open a reminder from either unpaid invoice, or press Open from Code. The same dialog shows that invoice, and the console logs how it closed.

demos.heading: Presentation
demos.intro: Style `data-presentation` to support both layouts. The sheet manages its own position and movement, so do not apply the centered dialog’s translation to it. `--sheet-backdrop` styles the dimmed page when no Backdrop part is present.
demos.caption: Open Edit Profile as a sheet. On a touch screen, drag it down to dismiss it, or use Cancel or Save Changes.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Every part takes a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state, and the `children` snippet receives the state too.
demos.caption: Open View Details. The trigger's label and the description come from their state, and Close renders as a link.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A drawer gives a task its own sheet without leaving the page. It shares Dialog’s focus and dismissal behavior, then adds dragging, snap points, and a handle you can use with the keyboard.
demos.caption: Open the drawer, adjust the daily goal, then Submit or Cancel. You can also press Escape, press outside, or drag the sheet toward its edge to close it.

demos.heading: Scrollable Content
demos.intro: Put long content in an inner `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto` area. A downward drag scrolls that area first; when it reaches the top, the same gesture can move the drawer. `initialFocus="content"` starts focus on the sheet itself.
demos.caption: Open the long sheet and scroll its text. At the top, drag downward to move the sheet; on a keyboard, Tab reaches the controls and Escape closes it.

demos.heading: Sides
demos.intro: Side drawers can opt into `preventEdgeSwipe` to keep an edge gesture from starting iOS Safari’s back or forward navigation. It also prevents clicks right at those edges, so use it only when you need that tradeoff.
demos.caption: Open a sheet from each edge. Drag it back toward that edge, press outside, or press Escape to close it.

demos.heading: Snap Points
demos.intro: For a sheet with one snap point, use a decorative bar instead of an inactive button.
demos.caption: Open the sheet at its middle snap point. Drag it, press the handle, or Tab to the handle and use Up, Down, Home and End to try the other resting points.

demos.heading: Modal
demos.intro: `modal` has the same choices as Dialog: `true` blocks the page, `"trap-focus"` keeps Tab inside while leaving the page usable, and `false` allows focus to leave. A click on the page also closes a `"trap-focus"` drawer, while a non-modal drawer closes on an outside press only when `closeOnOutsidePress` is enabled.
demos.caption: Open directions at the small snap point and choose another place behind the sheet. Expand it to make the sheet modal, then collapse it to use the page again.

demos.heading: Nested Drawers
demos.intro: A drawer opened inside another joins its stack. Escape and outside presses affect the topmost one; closing a parent closes its children. `--drawer-stack` follows the sheets above it as they open and drag, so a parent can scale back with `[scale:calc(1-var(--drawer-stack)*0.04)]`.
demos.caption: Open Account, then Change Password. The parent steps back as the child opens; Escape closes one sheet at a time.

demos.heading: Outlets
demos.intro: An Outlet makes another element follow the sheet’s progress. Its `keyframes` run from collapsed to fully expanded; this example scales and rounds the inbox behind a compose sheet. An outlet outside the drawer connects through its controller.
demos.caption: Open Compose, then drag the sheet slowly. The inbox behind it scales and rounds with the sheet’s progress.

demos.heading: Action Sheet
demos.intro: Put the least risky action first because a keyboard or code open starts there. Use an Alert Dialog when a choice needs confirmation.
demos.caption: Open Photo Options and choose an action. The console logs the returned value; dismissing the sheet counts as Cancel.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A field connects a form control to its label, its description and the errors it shows, and wires up `id`, `for` and `aria-describedby` for you.
demos.caption: Press Username to focus the input, then type a name.

demos.heading: Validation
demos.intro: Leave an error empty to show the browser's message, or use `match="valueMissing"` and `match="typeMismatch"` for your own messages. Adding an error part replaces the browser's validation bubble with that message in the page.
demos.caption: Press Subscribe with an empty or invalid email, then correct it to clear the error.

demos.heading: Field Sets
demos.intro: A field set groups related fields under a legend, and disables them together.
demos.caption: Move through the address fields. Their legend and description name the group.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A file input holds the files someone chooses, drops, or pastes, checks them against your rules, and submits them with a form. Uploading them to a server is up to your app.
demos.caption: Browse Files or drop a few files on the zone, then remove one. Tab to the list to move between files with the arrow keys, and press Delete to remove the focused one.

demos.heading: Page-Wide Drop
demos.intro: Set `target="document"` to take files dropped anywhere on the page. The zone shows `data-dragging` while a file is over the window, so it can be a full-page overlay. A drop on another zone stays with that zone.
demos.caption: Drag a file over this page to see the overlay, then drop it. The file joins the Attachments list; a drop on the first example's zone stays there.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A hover card shows a preview of where a link goes, like a person's profile, to someone who pauses on it. The link still works as a link.
demos.caption: Hover @hollis, or Tab to it and wait, to open Hollis Grant's profile preview. Move the pointer away or press Escape to close it.

demos.heading: Positioning
demos.intro: `HoverCardArrow` follows the side the card actually lands on, including after a flip, and gets the same `data-side`. It points at the middle of the link and keeps `arrowPadding` away from the corners; `data-arrow-clamped` tells you when it can't reach the middle.
demos.caption: Choose a side and an alignment, then hover @ines. The card opens there and its arrow points at the link.

demos.heading: Aspect Ratio
demos.intro: Set `aspectRatio` to keep the crop's width over its height, like `1` for a square or `16 / 9`. Changing it fits the crop to the new ratio about its middle. Without one, the crop is free, and holding Shift while dragging a handle keeps its current ratio. `minWidth` and `minHeight` stop it getting too small, in image pixels.
demos.caption: Choose Square or Wide, then drag an edge. Flip mirrors the image and the crop with it.

demos.heading: Frame Mode
demos.intro: `shape="circle"` rounds the selection, but the crop is still its box, so pass `shape: "circle"` to `cropImage` too. Here, Save Avatar crops a 128 pixel round file:
demos.caption: Drag the image or move the zoom, then press Save Avatar. The new avatar shows beside the button.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: An input is a native text field for short values like a name, an email address or a search. It works inside a field and a form, and adds a clear button, text around the input, and change reasons.
demos.caption: Edit the website, then press Clear website. The text clears, focus returns to the input and the console logs the reason. Pressing https:// focuses the input too.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A plain `<label>` only reaches inputs, buttons and selects. Label names any control by its `for`, including a radio group or a slider, and a press on the label moves focus into it.
demos.caption: Press Shipping speed. Focus moves to the checked option, and a screen reader names the group Shipping speed.

demos.heading: Slider
demos.intro: A label for a slider names its thumb, so the thumb reads as **Volume**, and a press on the label focuses it.
demos.caption: Press Volume, then use the arrow keys. The thumb moves, and a screen reader reads it as Volume.

demos.heading: Switch
demos.intro: Point the label at a switch beside it. A press on the label turns the switch on and off.
demos.caption: Press Email me product updates. The switch turns on.

demos.heading: Wrapping a Control
demos.intro: Put the control inside the label instead of pointing at it, and you need no `id`.
demos.caption: Press Accept terms and conditions. The checkbox checks, and a double click doesn't select the text.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Listbox when the choices should stay in view. It works like a native select with several visible rows, with keyboard navigation, typeahead, and optional range selection.
demos.caption: Choose Comments, then hold Shift and choose New sign-ins to select the range. A click replaces the selection; Ctrl or ⌘ adds one option.

demos.heading: Multiple
demos.intro: Changing a Shift range preserves the options selected before that range began.
demos.caption: Choose Basil, then hold Shift and choose Pepper to select a range. Use Ctrl+A or ⌘A to select every option, then again to clear. The console logs each change.

demos.heading: Selection That Follows Focus
demos.intro: Taps and screen-reader presses toggle an option instead, since they do not have modifier keys.
demos.caption: Choose index.ts to replace the selection. Hold Ctrl or Cmd while choosing another file to add it; Shift selects a range.

demos.heading: Manual Activation
demos.intro: Set `activation="manual"` on a single list to browse without selecting. Space, Enter, or a press chooses the focused option.
demos.caption: Move through the options with the arrow keys. Nothing is selected until you press Space or Enter, and the console logs the choice.

demos.heading: Deselectable
demos.intro: Add `deselectable` to let pressing the selected option clear a single selection. Without it, the selection stays as it is.
demos.caption: Press Astro again to clear the selection, or choose another framework. The console logs each change.

demos.heading: Groups
demos.intro: Use `ListboxGroup` and `ListboxGroupLabel` to name a group. Arrow keys and ranges continue across groups. Separators stay out of the accessibility tree.
demos.caption: Move from Apple through the list with Down Arrow. Navigation continues into the Vegetables group.

demos.heading: Icons
demos.intro: Wrap an icon in `ListboxItemIcon` so screen readers and typeahead skip it. Add `mirror` to a directional icon to flip it in right-to-left text.
demos.caption: Choose Drafts. The icon stays out of the option’s accessible name and the text used for typeahead.

demos.heading: Horizontal
demos.intro: The list reads `dir="rtl"` from the page or an ancestor, so Left Arrow moves to the next option in right-to-left text.
demos.caption: Focus M, then use Left and Right Arrow to choose a size. The list stops at its ends; XL cannot be selected.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: A disabled option cannot be selected. Arrow keys, typeahead and ranges skip it. Disabling the whole list removes its tab stop, prevents changes, and excludes its value from the form.
demos.caption: Try choosing Olive. Then press Disable the List to make every option unavailable until you enable it again.

demos.heading: Read-Only
demos.intro: Use `readOnly` when people should be able to browse the list without changing its value. The list remains focusable and its value still submits.
demos.caption: Move focus through the frameworks. Nuxt stays selected because the list is read-only.

demos.heading: Form
