demos.intro: The list can live outside its form: set `form` to the form’s ID, as this example does. A disabled fieldset also disables the list. Forms covers the shared integration.
demos.caption: Choose Basil and press Order: the console logs both toppings. Reset restores Extra cheese; clearing every option makes the required list block the order.

demos.heading: Object Values
demos.intro: Pass objects as item values when the selection should carry more than an ID. `itemToValue` provides the string used for identity and form submission; `isItemEqualToValue` matches objects that represent the same option but are different instances.
demos.caption: Choose Team. The console logs the price from the selected object, not from its string ID.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: A controller can select all options, clear the selection, or focus the list from another control. Create one with `createListboxController()` and pass it as `controller`. Controllers covers setup and lifetime.
demos.caption: Press Select All, Clear and Focus. Each button drives the same list through its controller, and the console logs the change.

demos.heading: Scrollable
demos.intro: Give a long list a maximum height and `overflow-y: auto`. It starts scrolled to the selected option without taking focus. Keyboard navigation reveals the focused option without scrolling the page.
demos.caption: Focus the list and use the arrow keys. Options scroll into view, and the console logs the focused time zone.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Render an option as a link when choosing it should navigate. A press or Enter follows the link and selects the option. This example uses manual activation so arrow keys only browse.
demos.caption: Focus Remix and press Enter, or choose it with the pointer. The option is selected and its link updates the URL hash.

demos.heading: Submenus
demos.intro: Nest a Sub, SubTrigger, and SubContent to add another level. Hover or press the arrow key toward a submenu to open it. The menu lets a pointer travel diagonally into the submenu without accidentally choosing an item it passes over. Escape closes only the submenu and returns focus to its trigger, as the menu pattern asks.
demos.caption: Open Edit, then Find or Transform. Use the arrows to enter and leave each level; choosing an action closes the menu tree.

demos.heading: Shortcuts
demos.intro: In markup, this is a hint: your app owns the key handler. Data menus also register their shortcuts while closed. Letters and digits match physical keys, including combinations such as Option+N.
demos.caption: Open File to see shortcut hints for your platform. Choose an item to report its action; this markup example does not register global shortcuts.

demos.heading: Icons
demos.intro: `data-has-icon` on items and `data-has-icons` on the menu let text line up when only some items have icons.
demos.caption: Open Share and type an item’s name. The icons aren’t part of the item’s accessible name or the text typeahead matches.

demos.heading: Checkboxes
demos.intro: Checkbox items toggle independently and stay open by default. Use `bind:checked`, or `defaultChecked` for an uncontrolled item. An ItemIndicator renders the check; `keepMounted` preserves its space while unchecked. Style `data-checked` and `data-unchecked` for each state.
demos.caption: Open View and toggle Status bar or Minimap. The menu stays open so you can change several settings, and the console logs each one.

demos.heading: Radio Group
demos.intro: Radio items choose one value in their group and stay open by default. Use `bind:value`, or `defaultValue` for an uncontrolled group. Give the group a `name` when it should identify itself in the menu’s value-change callback.
demos.caption: Open Panel and choose a position. Only one item in each group is checked, the menu stays open, and the console logs the change.

demos.heading: Context Menu
demos.intro: Set `disabled` to leave that area’s native browser menu available. Context triggers can pass a payload too.
demos.caption: Right-click or long-press the area, or focus it and press Shift+F10. Choose an action and the console logs it.

demos.heading: Disabled Items
demos.intro: Disabled items remain focusable so people can discover them, but cannot run or open a submenu. A disabled Trigger is a native disabled button and cannot receive focus. Add `focusableWhenDisabled` to keep it in the tab order, so it can host a tooltip that says why; presses still do nothing.
demos.caption: Open Document and move through its items with the arrow keys. Disabled actions remain discoverable but cannot run; Locked cannot open a menu.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: The menu stays mounted through an exit animation. `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style`, `data-side`, and `--transform-origin` describe the transition. `keepMounted` leaves the closed content hidden afterward; `onOpenChangeComplete` reports when it finishes.
demos.caption: Open Animated, then its More tools submenu, and close them. The console logs Opening or Closing, then when the animation finishes.

demos.heading: Presentation
demos.intro: Use `data-presentation` or the content’s `presentation` state for the two layouts. Leave a sheet’s translation to the SDK. `--sheet-backdrop` sets its dimming color, and the sheet is modal unless `modal` is false. The popup guide covers shared presentation behavior.
demos.caption: Open Options as a sheet, enter Move to, then go back or choose a destination. You can drag downward to dismiss the sheet.

demos.heading: Triggers Outside the Menu
demos.intro: Connect external triggers and one menu to a `createMenuController<File>()`. Each trigger passes its row as `payload`, which the content reads from its state. Only the active trigger is expanded and receives focus back. Code can also open with a `payload` and `anchor`; the Promise resolves when the menu closes.
demos.caption: Open the actions for different files. One menu shows the active row; opening from code uses the same payload and reports the closing reason.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Wrap a few Menus in a Menubar to connect their triggers. Tab enters the bar once; arrow keys move between menus, and pointing at another trigger switches an open menu.
demos.caption: Tab into the bar and use Left and Right to choose a menu, or point at another trigger once one is open. File has submenus, Edit has shortcuts, and View has checkboxes and an appearance choice. The console logs each one.

demos.heading: Submenu
demos.intro: A submenu still uses Menu’s Sub, SubTrigger, and SubContent. The arrow toward it enters that level. On an ordinary item, the same arrow can move to the next top-level menu instead.
demos.caption: Open File and enter Share with the arrow key. Go back to File, then move to Edit without leaving the menubar.

demos.heading: Vertical
demos.intro: Set `orientation="vertical"` to move between triggers with Up and Down. The arrow toward the popup opens it; the arrow back closes it and returns to the trigger.
demos.caption: Use Up and Down to choose Inbox, Drafts, or Archive. Right opens its menu in left-to-right text; Left returns to its trigger.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Meter for a value within a known range, such as storage used, a battery level or an account quota. It fills a track to show the value, and screen readers announce the same value.
demos.caption: Read the storage meter. The label names it, and both the visible value and screen reader value report 68%.

demos.heading: Bounds
demos.intro: `min` and `max` set the range. They default to 0 and 100. A value outside the range is clamped for the fill, the percentage and `aria-valuenow`, but the state's `value` and a format other than percent keep it as you passed it. Here, 720 sits about 76% of the way from 300 to 850. Decimal formatting keeps the visible value as 720.
demos.caption: Compare the score with the filled track. The number shows 720; the fill shows its position between 300 and 850.

demos.heading: Format and Locale
demos.intro: Pass `Intl.NumberFormat` options to `format` for units, currency, or decimal places. A function can return custom text, such as the number of occupied seats.
demos.caption: Compare the readings. Each meter formats its own value as a unit, currency, custom text, or localized percentage.

demos.heading: Value Label
demos.intro: Use `getValueLabel` when a screen reader needs more context than the visible number. It receives the value and details containing `formatted`, `percent`, `min`, and `max`.
demos.caption: Read API requests with a screen reader. It announces 750 of 1000 requests and 75%, while the visible value stays compact.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Navigation Menu for a site's main links, grouped into panels that open from a row of triggers. For a list of actions, use a Menu.
demos.caption: Open each section, then use Tab or the arrow keys to move through its links.

demos.heading: Link Component
demos.intro: Render the router's link component with the `render` snippet, with `{...props}`. SvelteKit links are plain `<a>` elements, which the link part already is.
demos.caption: Choose a link to update the current page without reloading the example.

demos.heading: Vertical
demos.intro: `orientation="vertical"` is for a sidebar: Up and Down move between the items, and panels open beside the menu, at the inline end, unless `side` says otherwise.
demos.caption: Use Up and Down between the sidebar items, then open a panel beside its trigger.

demos.heading: Click Only
demos.intro: Resting the pointer on a trigger opens its panel. With `openOnHover` set to false, the menu opens on click only: pressing a trigger opens and closes its panel, and moving the pointer does nothing. Keyboard and touch work the same either way.
demos.caption: Click a trigger to open it. Moving the pointer between triggers does not open another panel.

demos.heading: Nested
demos.intro: A navigation menu inside another menu's content is a submenu. It renders a plain element instead of a second `<nav>` landmark, gets `data-nested`, and closes with its parent when the parent moves on to another item. Without a viewport of its own, its panels open beside its triggers. Pressing a link in it closes every menu.
demos.caption: Open Components, then open Overlays or Forms. Escape closes the inner panel first.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: `onOpenChangeComplete` runs once the menu has finished opening or closing, after any animation, with the new open state. Switching between items doesn't count.
demos.caption: Switch between Guides and Components to see the viewport resize and the panels slide.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.caption: Open Guides to see its render state, then compare the current link and disabled trigger.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Number Input for quantities, prices and measurements. It keeps a numeric value while showing formatted text, and steps it with the keyboard, the step buttons, or a drag on its label.
demos.caption: Drag the Quantity label sideways to scrub the value, or click it to focus the input. Type a number, press ArrowUp or ArrowDown, or hold a step button. The console logs the value once each change is committed.

demos.heading: Field
demos.intro: Wrap the number input in Field to give it a visible label and a description.
demos.caption: Click Tickets to focus the input, then type or step its value. Screen readers read the description with the field.

demos.heading: Min and Max
demos.intro: Use `min` and `max` to set bounds. A step button disables at its bound. Typed values outside the bounds are clamped when committed.
demos.caption: Change Guests between 1 and 8. Type 20 and press Enter to clamp it to 8. At either bound, that direction's step button is disabled.

demos.heading: Step and Large Step
demos.intro: `step` sets the usual increment, and defaults to 1. Steps are measured from `min`, or from zero when no minimum is set. When they don't land on `max`, End and the increment button stop at the highest step below it, so stepping keeps the value on the step grid, as Slider does. Shift, Page Up and Page Down use `largeStep`, ten steps by default, and Alt (Option) with an arrow key uses `smallStep`, a tenth of a step. Keyboard lists every key.
demos.caption: Step Hours by 0.25. Hold Shift to move by 1, or hold Alt (Option) with an arrow key to move by 0.05. Home and End go to 0 and 24.

demos.heading: Format
demos.intro: Pass `Intl.NumberFormat` options through `format`. The input displays and parses that format while keeping a numeric value. For percentages, `0.15` is displayed as `15%`, and `step` defaults to the smallest percent the format shows: `0.01` for whole percents, `0.0001` with two fraction digits.
demos.caption: Edit Price, Discount, or Weight and leave the field to format it. Try entering 5 in Price or 25% in Discount, then use the step buttons.

demos.heading: Locale
demos.intro: Set `locale` to choose separators, currency symbols, and grouping. Without it, the input follows the page's language or the browser's language after mounting. Server markup uses English when no locale is provided; set a locale explicitly when that first render matters.
demos.caption: Edit Preis using a comma for decimals, or step Budget to see Indian digit grouping. The displayed and accepted formats follow each field's locale.

demos.heading: Mouse Wheel
demos.intro: Set `wheel` to step with the mouse wheel while the input is focused. It is off by default.
demos.caption: Focus Font size and scroll over it to change the value. Move focus away and scroll again; the value stays unchanged.

demos.heading: Scrub Area
demos.intro: `NumberInputScrubArea` changes the value while you drag it. The handle can be any element inside the number input: the label, as in the first example, or a letter or icon inside the group, as in a design tool. Right and up increase the value. `orientation` chooses an axis, and `pixelsPerStep` controls how far the pointer moves per step. Shift and Alt (Option) use the large and small increments.
demos.caption: Drag the X, Y, W or H letter sideways to change that value. Hold Shift for larger steps or Alt (Option) for smaller ones. The console logs each value when the drag ends.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind `value` with `bind:value`, and use `onValueChange` for the reason. `onValueChange` reports valid changes while an interaction is in progress. `onValueCommit` runs when typing is committed, a step key or button is released, or a scrub ends. Use the commit event for work that should happen after the interaction.
demos.caption: Hold a Servings step button. The console logs each value as it changes, then one Committed line when you let go. Clear sets the value to null, and Reset to 4 restores it.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: Create a `createNumberInputController()` and pass it as `controller` to change or focus the input from other controls. `increment()` and `decrement()` step the value; pass `{ large: true }` for a large step. `setValue()`, `getValue()`, and `focus()` cover direct updates and inspection.
demos.caption: Press Zoom In and Zoom Out to move by 100%, then Actual Size to restore 100%. Read logs the current value, and Focus moves into the field.

demos.heading: Form
demos.intro: A hidden input submits the plain numeric value under `name`. Formatting does not change form data: a displayed amount of $4.50 still submits `4.5`. Empty values submit an empty string.
demos.caption: Change Quantity or Tip and press Save: the console logs the plain numeric values. Gift cards belongs to the same form through its form ID. Reset restores the defaults.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Every part takes a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state, and the `children` snippet receives the state. Here the decrement button adds a tooltip, and the increment button shows Max once the value reaches its bound.
demos.caption: Press End in Temperature to jump to 40°C. The increment button reads Max; hover the decrement button to see its tooltip.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use an OTP Input for a short code sent by text or email, like a sign-in or verification code. Each character gets its own slot, and a pasted or autofilled code fills them all at once.
demos.caption: Type a six-digit code or paste 123-456. Click a slot to edit it, use the arrow keys to move, and use your usual undo shortcut to undo a change.

demos.heading: Four Digits
demos.intro: Set `maxLength` to the code's length and render that many slots. The default length is six.
demos.caption: Enter four digits in PIN. Once it is full, typing another digit replaces the selected slot. Click another slot to edit it.

demos.heading: Alphanumeric
demos.intro: Set `pattern` to `digits`, `letters`, or `alphanumeric`. The default is `digits`. The pattern filters characters and selects a suitable keyboard on touch devices.
demos.caption: Type letters and digits into Recovery code, or paste ab12-cd34. The hyphen is removed and the eight characters fill the slots.

demos.heading: Custom Pattern
demos.intro: Pass a regular expression, such as `/[0-9A-F]/i` to accept hexadecimal characters. Use `inputMode` to choose the keyboard separately. The example displays letters in uppercase without changing their stored case.
demos.caption: Try typing 12zzab into Device code. The z characters are rejected; the accepted value is 12ab, displayed as 12AB.

demos.heading: Validation
demos.intro: Inside a Field, pass `invalid` when your code rejects the value, such as a code the server didn't accept. The field marks the input with `aria-invalid` and connects its `FieldError`. Outside a field, pass `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` yourself.
demos.caption: Verification code is marked invalid, and the error below explains why. Edit any digit to clear the error.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Use `bind:value` to bind the code. `onValueChange` also receives the change details. Call `details.cancel()` in the change callback to reject a change. Incoming values are filtered by the pattern and limited to `maxLength`, just like typed values.
demos.caption: Enter, paste, or delete digits in One-time password. The console logs each new code and its reason.

demos.heading: On Complete
demos.intro: `onValueCommit` runs when a change fills every slot, including typing, paste, autofill, and controller writes. Changing an already-full code runs it again. Form resets and page restoration do not.
demos.caption: Fill all six slots. The console logs the complete code and the change reason. Replace a digit to log it again; deleting one logs nothing.

demos.heading: Forms
demos.intro: Set `name` to include the code in `FormData`. `required` blocks an empty code, and a partial code fails length validation. Reset restores the default value. Use `form` to associate a control outside the form with its ID.
demos.caption: Choose Verify with an empty or partial code to see validation. Enter all six digits and choose Verify to log the form values. Recovery code sits outside the form but submits with it. Reset clears both fields.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Navigate pages with buttons, links, or your router.
demos.caption: Choose a page, or use Previous and Next. The console logs each page and its reason, and the step at either end stays focusable as a button.

demos.heading: Total and Page Size
demos.intro: A page past the end, like after the count shrinks, reads as the last page.
demos.caption: Choose a page, then change Rows per page. The console logs each change, and a new size starts again at page 1.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Every part takes a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state: whether a link is `current`, and for a step, the `page` it goes to and whether it's `disabled`. The `children` snippet receives the state too.
demos.caption: Choose a page. The current page widens to say Page 3, and each arrow shows the page it goes to.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A Password Input is a native password field with a button that shows and hides what's typed. It keeps the caret in place, offers the right password to password managers, and hides the password again when its form submits.
demos.caption: Type a password, then choose Show password to reveal or hide it. Clicking the toggle keeps the caret in the field. With a keyboard, Tab to the toggle and press Space or Enter.

demos.heading: New Password
demos.intro: The example derives a checklist from the current value. Those rules belong to the example; the component does not impose a password policy.
demos.caption: Type a password and watch the checklist update. Try adding digits and both uppercase and lowercase letters, then toggle its visibility.

demos.heading: Shown at First
demos.intro: Set `defaultVisible` to start with the text visible, and `defaultValue` for its initial value. This can be useful for a Wi-Fi password someone needs to read or copy.
demos.caption: Read the Wi-Fi password, then choose Show password to hide it. Choose it again to reveal the value.

demos.heading: Caps Lock
demos.intro: Use `data-capslock` or the part's `capsLock` state for a warning. It updates from key events while the input is focused. The example reserves space for the icon and warning.
demos.caption: Focus Password and press Caps Lock. The warning appears while Caps Lock is on. Turn it off or leave the field to hide the warning.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Set `disabled` on the root, its Field, or an enclosing fieldset to disable both the input and the toggle. The value is omitted from form submission.
demos.caption: Try to edit Password or press its toggle. Both controls are disabled and are skipped by Tab.

demos.heading: Read-Only
demos.intro: Set `readOnly` when the value can be read but not edited. The input stays focusable, the toggle still works, and the value still participates in form submission.
demos.caption: Choose Show recovery key to read it. Try to type in the input; its value stays unchanged.

demos.heading: Controlled Visibility
demos.intro: Bind `visible` with `bind:visible` to control visibility, and use `onVisibleChange` for the details. The reason distinguishes a toggle press, form submission, reset, page hide, or a controller action.
demos.caption: Toggle Show password. The console logs each change and its reason.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: Create a `createPasswordInputController()` and pass it as `controller` for actions outside the input. Read or change the value, toggle visibility, or focus the input. Writes use the `imperative` reason.
demos.caption: Choose Suggest to fill and reveal a sample value. Try Toggle, Read, Clear, and Focus to call each action from outside the field.

demos.heading: Forms
demos.intro: The native input participates in `FormData`, validation, and reset. Use `form` to associate it with a form elsewhere in the page, as this example does.
demos.caption: Enter an email and password, reveal the password, then press Enter in the field. Submission hides it again, and the console logs its length. Reset clears the form. Empty required fields block submission.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A popover keeps a small task close to the thing it belongs to. Put fields, buttons, or other interactive content inside; it handles placement, focus, and dismissal.
demos.caption: Press Share to open the popover, then close it with Cancel, Copy Link, Escape, or a press outside. Focus returns to Share.

demos.heading: Forms
demos.intro: An ordinary form can save a value and then close the popover. Focus starts on the first field and returns to the trigger when the task finishes. A form with `method="dialog"` closes on submission and returns its submit button's value; the row editor shows that version.
demos.caption: Open Edit Profile, change the name, and press Save. The popover closes and the console logs the saved name.

demos.heading: Keep It Open While Editing
demos.intro: Set `dismissible` to false while there is unsaved work. Escape and outside presses then keep the popover open and report `onDismissAttempt`, so you can ask whether to discard it. Focus leaving is refused quietly. The trigger, Close parts, and controller can still close it.
demos.caption: Open Add Note, type something, then press Escape or click outside. Keep Editing returns to the field; Discard closes the popover and clears the note.

demos.heading: Placement
demos.intro: `side` chooses an edge of the trigger, `bottom` by default, and `align` lines the popover up with its start, center, or end. Start and end follow text direction. The popover flips or shifts when the requested position doesn't fit, and `data-side` and `data-align` report where it landed. The popup guide covers the shared positioning options.
demos.caption: Choose a side and an alignment, then open Delivery. Near a window edge, the popover flips or shifts to stay visible.

demos.heading: Offsets
demos.intro: `sideOffset` is the gap to the trigger, 4 pixels by default. `alignOffset` shifts the popover along the trigger's edge, and `collisionPadding` is the space kept from the edges of the window.
demos.caption: Change the offsets and the padding, then open Delivery. The popover moves away from the trigger and along it.

demos.heading: Arrow
demos.intro: `PopoverArrow` follows the side the popover actually uses, including after a flip, and gets the same `data-side`. `arrowPadding` keeps it away from the corners; `data-arrow-clamped` tells you when it can't point at the middle of the trigger. This example cancels dismissal when you press its side buttons, so the open arrow can move.
demos.caption: Open Help, then press Top, Right, Bottom, or Left. The popover stays open while it and its arrow move to that side.

demos.heading: Anchor
demos.intro: Set `anchor` to position against something other than the trigger. It accepts an element, a selector, a point such as `{ x, y }`, or an object with `getBoundingClientRect()`, such as a text range. The position is read again as the anchor moves.
demos.caption: Press the filters button. The popover lines up with the search field instead of the small button beside it.

demos.heading: Modal
demos.intro: `modal` controls how the popover shares the page:
demos.caption: Choose a mode, open Add Comment, and try Tab or clicking the page.

demos.heading: Focus
demos.intro: Use `initialFocus` to choose the first focused element, or `"none"` to leave focus where it is. `finalFocus` controls where focus returns. Opening on hover leaves focus alone; opening with touch focuses the panel itself so no on-screen keyboard appears. See popup focus for the shared focus rules.
demos.caption: Open each one: Rename focuses its field, Publish focuses its Publish button, and Status leaves focus on the trigger.

demos.heading: Open on Hover
demos.intro: `openOnHover` adds pointer opening while keeping click, keyboard, and touch activation. `delay` and `closeDelay` control the pause before opening and closing. You can cross the gap into the content and interact with it.
demos.caption: Hover @kofi, then move into the popover and press Follow. You can also open it by pressing the trigger.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Use `bind:open` to keep the popover's state in your component. Cancel a proposed change with `details.cancel()` in `onOpenChange`. See state and events for the common change contract.
demos.caption: Check Open or press Set Status, then close the popover. The console logs each change and its reason.

demos.heading: Keyboard Shortcut
demos.intro: Set a trigger's `shortcut` to toggle the popover from the keyboard. `mod+i` means Command+I on Apple platforms and Control+I elsewhere. The Shortcut part displays the platform's keys, and the trigger advertises them through `aria-keyshortcuts`.
demos.caption: Press Command+I or Control+I to open Invite. Press the same shortcut again, or Escape, to close it.

demos.heading: Triggers Outside the Popover
demos.intro: `controller.open({ payload, anchor })` opens it from code and returns a promise with the closing reason and any `returnValue`. The payload stays available during the exit animation. See controllers for the shared pattern.
demos.caption: Edit Inès Moreau or Kofi Mensah and save a new role. The owner can't be edited. Edit Newest Member opens the same editor from code, and the console logs how it closed.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: The content has `data-starting-style` while it opens and `data-ending-style` while it closes. Transition from those states, and the popover stays mounted until the exit finishes. `onOpenChangeComplete` runs after the transition, and `keepMounted` keeps the closed content in the page, hidden. See styling and animation for the common lifecycle.
demos.caption: Open What's New, then press Got It. The console logs Opening, Open, Closing, and Closed.

demos.heading: Presentation
demos.intro: Style `data-presentation` for both layouts. The sheet manages its own position and movement, so leave its translation alone and avoid the floating panel's fixed width. `--sheet-backdrop` sets the dim behind it.
demos.caption: Open Add Reminder as a sheet. Dismiss it with Cancel, Save, Escape, the dimmed area, or a downward swipe on a touch screen.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Every part takes a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state, and the `children` snippet receives the state too. The content's `children` snippet can read its payload, as the row editor does.
demos.caption: Open Show Updates. The trigger's label comes from its state, the title renders as an h3, and Close renders as a link.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: `Preferences` puts your preferences on `data-*` attributes and keeps them up to date. Use it around a part of your app, or apply a preference to the whole page.
demos.caption: Choose Grid, then reload the page. The files come back in the view you chose, and the console logs each change.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Show a task’s progress, or an indeterminate state while its progress is unknown.
demos.caption: Read the export bar. Its label and 60% value are available both visually and to a screen reader.

demos.heading: Indeterminate
demos.intro: The indicator has no inline width in this state. This example sweeps a short highlight across the track, and shows a still, full-width fill when reduced motion is on.
demos.caption: Read the Connecting to server bar. It shows an ongoing task without announcing a percentage.

demos.heading: Changing the Value
demos.intro: Pass the latest `value` as your task progresses. The parts get `data-progressing` while the value is below `max`, and `data-complete` when it reaches the end.
demos.caption: Click Upload Next to add one photo, or 20%, and watch the console count them. At 100%, the button stops advancing the bar. Click Reset to start at 0%.

demos.heading: Bounds
demos.intro: `min` and `max` default to 0 and 100. A value outside that range is clamped for the fill, the percentage and `aria-valuenow`, but the state's `value` and a format other than percent keep it as you passed it. A value of 3 between 1 and 5 fills half the track.
demos.caption: Compare step 3 of 5 with the fill. Because the range starts at 1, the value is halfway through the range.

demos.heading: Format and Locale
demos.intro: Pass `Intl.NumberFormat` options to `format` for units or decimal places. A function can return custom text, such as the time remaining.
demos.caption: Compare the progress readings. They show downloaded data, a precise percentage, time remaining, and a localized percentage.

demos.heading: Value Label
demos.intro: Use `getValueLabel` to give screen readers more context than the visible number. Its details include `formatted`, `percent`, `min`, and `max`. Handle a `null` value when the task can be indeterminate; `percent` is also `null` and `formatted` is empty then.
demos.caption: Read Copying files with a screen reader. It announces 3 of 12 files and 25%, while the visible value stays compact.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use radios for a short list of choices where only one can be picked, like a shipping speed or a plan. The group keeps one value and gives the whole list a single tab stop.
demos.caption: Choose Express, then use the arrow keys to move the selection between speeds.

demos.heading: Description
demos.intro: Put each radio in its own `Field` with a `FieldLabel` and `FieldDescription` when an option needs more explanation. That field connects both to its radio, while the outer field still names the group.
demos.caption: Choose Weekly digest by its label. Each radio is also described by the line under it.

demos.heading: Choice Card
demos.intro: Wrap an option's content in its label to make the whole card clickable. `:has([data-checked])` lets the card reflect the radio inside it.
demos.caption: Click anywhere on the Pro card to choose it. Arrow keys move the selection between cards too.

demos.heading: Fieldset and Legend
demos.intro: Use `FieldSet` and `FieldLegend` to describe a set of choices together. Connect the group to the legend with `aria-labelledby`, and to the description with `aria-describedby`.
demos.caption: Choose Yearly. The legend and the line under it describe both billing periods.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Set `disabled` on the group or on one radio. Disabled radios can't be focused or checked, and arrow keys skip them. A disabled fieldset disables the group too, and a disabled group submits nothing.
demos.caption: The Theme group is disabled. In Backups, Hourly is disabled, so the arrow keys move between Daily and Weekly.

demos.heading: Read-Only
demos.intro: Set `readOnly` on the group to keep its value while still letting people focus and read the options. Arrow keys move focus without checking anything, and the value still submits with a form.
demos.caption: Click Team, or focus Pro and press the Down arrow. Pro stays checked.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Use `bind:value` to own the value, and `onValueChange` for the reason. Call `details.cancel()` in the callback to keep the current value. A controller from `createRadioGroupController()` checks a radio from anywhere, like the Choose Team button below. Create one controller per mounted group.
demos.caption: Choose Starter, then press Choose Team. The console logs each change and its reason.

demos.heading: Form
demos.intro: Set `form` to a form's id to join it from elsewhere on the page, as this group does.
demos.caption: Choose Express and press Continue. The console logs the submitted value, and Reset returns the choice to Standard.

demos.heading: Validation
demos.intro: Put a required group in a Field with a `FieldError`. Submitting without a choice shows the error under the group and moves focus to it. The Forms guide covers the shared field behavior.
demos.caption: Press Save without a choice to see the error. Choose SMS only and save again; the console logs the saved value.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: `keepMounted` keeps the indicator in the page while unchecked, with `data-unchecked`. Here it lets a hovered option preview its dot.
demos.caption: Hover Light to preview its dot, then choose it. The dot scales in on Light and out of System.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: The group, radio and indicator take a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state. Keep the part's props on the interactive element so its role, label and keyboard behavior stay connected. See Parts and Composition for the rendering contract.
demos.caption: Choose Nothing. Each radio renders a full-width button that shows a check from its state.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a rating to collect a score, like how a stay went, or to show one, like an average. Each star is a radio, so it works like a radio group, with one value and a single tab stop.
demos.caption: Choose a star, then use the arrow keys to change the score.

demos.heading: Half Stars
demos.intro: Set `step={0.5}` to split each star in two. Each half is its own radio, named like "2.5 stars", and a press on the first half of a star picks the half score.
demos.caption: Choose the first half of a star. Its star fills halfway.

demos.heading: Deselectable
demos.intro: Set `deselectable` to let people clear their score: a press on the checked star, or Space on it, sets the score back to `null`.
demos.caption: Press the fourth star. The score clears.

demos.heading: Read-Only
demos.intro: Name a read-only rating with `getValueLabel`, so its name includes the score. An `aria-label` would replace it.
demos.caption: An average of 4.2, named Rated 4.2 out of 5.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Set `disabled` to stop every star from being focused or changed. A disabled rating submits nothing.
demos.caption: The rating is disabled, so the stars can't be focused or pressed.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind `value` with `bind:value`, and pass `onValueChange` for the reason. Call `details.cancel()` in the callback to keep the current score. A controller from `createRatingController()` sets the score from anywhere, like the Clear Rating button below. Create one controller per mounted rating.
demos.caption: Choose a star, then press Clear Rating. The console logs each change and its reason.

demos.heading: Form
demos.intro: Each radio renders a hidden native radio, so the rating takes part in forms. Set `name` to submit the score; nothing submits without a name or a score. `required` blocks submission until there's a score, and a reset returns to `defaultValue`.
demos.caption: Press Send Review without a score to see the browser's message. Choose a star and send it again.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a resizable group to let people size the panes of a layout, like a file list beside an editor, by dragging the handle between them or with the keyboard.
demos.caption: Drag the handle beside Files, then the one between page.tsx and Terminal.

demos.heading: Vertical
demos.intro: Set `orientation="vertical"` to stack the panels, and give the group a height. ArrowUp and ArrowDown move the handle. Every part gets `data-orientation` with the group's direction, so a vertical group's handle is `[data-slot="resizable-handle"][data-orientation="vertical"]`.
demos.caption: Drag the handle between Inbox and Quarterly report, or focus it and use ArrowUp and ArrowDown.

demos.heading: Handle
demos.intro: Put anything inside a handle, like a grip that shows it can be dragged. The handle can stay a thin line: its hit area is at least 10 pixels across, centered on it, and 24 for touch, without any styles.
demos.caption: Grab the grip beside Channels, or focus the handle and use the arrow keys.

demos.heading: Collapsible
demos.intro: `collapsible` lets a panel collapse below its `minSize` to `collapsedSize`, 0 by default: by dragging past the midpoint to its collapsed size, with Enter or a double-click on its handle, or through the controller. Dragging back past the same point opens it at its minimum, and Enter restores the size it had. A collapsed panel gets `data-collapsed`, and at size 0 its content leaves the tab order and the accessibility tree.
demos.caption: Drag the sidebar closed to leave only its icons, or focus its handle and press Enter to collapse and restore it.

demos.heading: Sizes in Pixels
demos.intro: Sizes are percentages as numbers, or strings with `%`, `px` or `rem`. Pixel and rem bounds hold as the group resizes, so a navigation with `minSize="160px"` never gets narrower, and a change they cause reports the `resize` reason.
demos.caption: Resize Docs. It stays between 160 and 320 pixels wide, whatever the width of the group.

demos.heading: Default Layout
demos.intro: `defaultLayout` sets every panel's size at once, in order. Otherwise panels without `defaultSize` share what's left evenly.
demos.caption: The three mail panels start at 25, 35 and 40 percent. Resize any of them.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind `layout` with `bind:layout` to control the group, and pass `onLayoutChange` for the reason. The layout is one percentage per panel, in order, adding up to 100. Every change carries a reason, like `drag`, `step-key` or `collapse`, and `details.cancel()` keeps the current layout.
demos.caption: Resize Files to log the layout and its reason. Split Evenly and Reset set the layout from outside.

demos.heading: Saving on Complete
demos.intro: `onLayoutChange` runs on every frame of a drag. `onLayoutCommit` runs once, when the interaction that changed the layout ends: the pointer lifts, the key comes up, or a panel collapses. Save there.
demos.caption: Drag the handle and release it, or press an arrow key. The console logs the layout once, when you let go.

demos.heading: Persistence
demos.intro: It's the same idea as Preferences, which saves one choice between visits, like a theme. Resizable saves the whole layout, under its `autoSaveId`.
demos.caption: Resize Outline, then reload this page to restore its saved width.

demos.heading: Storage
demos.intro: This example keeps the layout in `sessionStorage`, for the tab's session:
demos.caption: Resize Messages, then reload. The width comes back in this tab, but not in a new one.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: A controller, from `createResizableController()`, collapses, expands and resizes panels from anywhere, by id or index, and reads the layout with `getLayout()`. Changes it makes report the `imperative` reason.
demos.caption: Use Collapse, Expand and 240px to move Files from outside the group, and Read to log its sizes.

demos.heading: Step Size
demos.intro: `step` sets how far an arrow key moves a handle, 1% by default, and `largeStep` how far Shift with an arrow moves it, 10% by default.
demos.caption: Focus the handle between Original and Changes. The arrow keys move it 5%, Shift with an arrow 25%, and Home and End as far as it goes.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: `disabled` on a handle fixes it in place. On the group it fixes every handle. Disabled handles leave the tab order, and their panels keep their sizes. A disabled `<fieldset>` around the group fixes every handle too.
demos.caption: The handle after Pinned stays fixed. Drag the one after Inbox, then check Lock layout to fix it too.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: The `render` and `children` snippets receive the part's state, like a panel's `size` and whether it's `collapsed`, or whether a handle is `dragging` or `hovering`. See Parts and Composition for the rendering contract.
demos.caption: Resize Files to see both panels report their size, or collapse it to see Collapsed.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a scroll area when content needs its own scrolling region with scrollbars that match your design. The browser still does the scrolling, so the wheel, touch, keyboard and find in page work as usual.
demos.caption: Scroll the tags with the wheel, the keyboard or the scrollbar thumb. The scrollbar shows while the pointer is over the list.

demos.heading: Horizontal
demos.intro: A horizontal scrollbar scrolls the inline axis. With one, the content grows as wide as it needs instead of wrapping. Here `type="auto"` keeps the scrollbar in view, so the row reads as one that scrolls.
demos.caption: Drag the scrollbar, or use Shift and the wheel, to scroll the palette from Sand to Ink.

demos.heading: Both Axes
demos.intro: With both scrollbars, each stops short of the corner where they meet, which `ScrollAreaCorner` fills.
demos.caption: Scroll the releases down and across. The header row stays in place, and the scrollbars stop short of the corner.

demos.heading: Edge Fades
demos.intro: These variables aren't inherited, so scrolling restyles the root and never the content. An element that reads one takes it from the root with `inherit`, like the fades here, which are children of the root: `--scroll-area-overflow-y-start: inherit`. The first scroll area registers the six names for the whole page with `CSS.registerProperty`. A page that needs them to inherit calls it first, with `inherits: true`. An `@property` rule can't, since a registration in script wins.
demos.caption: Scroll the release notes. The top fade grows in as you leave the top, and the bottom fade shrinks away at the end.

demos.heading: Native Scrollbars
demos.intro: Leave out the Scrollbar parts to keep the browser's own scrollbars, with everything else: data attributes, edge variables, sticking to the end and the controller.
demos.caption: Scroll the inbox with the browser's own scrollbar. The scroll area still tracks its edges and state.

demos.heading: When Scrollbars Show
demos.intro: Style the attribute: give the scrollbar `opacity: 0`, and `opacity: 1` under `[data-visible]`. A hidden scrollbar ignores the pointer, so it never catches presses meant for the content under it.
demos.caption: Hover and scroll each list to compare. The auto and always scrollbars show from the start; hover waits for the pointer and scroll for scrolling.

demos.heading: Hide Delay
demos.intro: With `"scroll"` and `"hover"`, `scrollHideDelay` keeps a scrollbar for a while after scrolling stops or the pointer leaves, in ms. It defaults to 600.
demos.caption: Scroll each list and stop. The scrollbar on the left hides at once; the one on the right waits 2000 milliseconds.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: A controller, from `createScrollAreaController()`, scrolls the area from anywhere and reads where it is. Pass it as `controller`.
demos.caption: Press Jump to the End, then Back to Top. The console logs each end of the list as the view reaches it.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Here the root renders a `section` and the viewport an `article`, and the root's `children` snippet reads its state to show a hint until you reach the end. See Parts and Composition for the rendering contract and State for each part's fields.
demos.caption: Scroll the releases. The hint under the list reads the root's state, changes once you leave the top, and disappears at the end.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a segmented control to switch between a few views or settings, like List and Grid. It works like a radio group, with one value and a single tab stop, and its indicator slides to the checked item.
demos.caption: Choose Grid, then use the arrow keys to move between views. The label above names the control, as in any field.

demos.heading: Vertical
demos.intro: Set `orientation="vertical"` to stack the items. Arrow keys on both axes still move between them, as in any radio group, and `data-orientation` on every part lets one stylesheet lay out both directions.
demos.caption: Choose Bottom, then press the Up arrow. The indicator follows down the column.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Set `disabled` on the control or on one item. Disabled items can't be focused or checked, and arrow keys skip them. A disabled control submits nothing.
demos.caption: The Theme control is disabled. In Billing period, Lifetime is disabled, so the arrow keys move between Monthly and Yearly.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind `value` with `bind:value`, and pass `onValueChange` for the reason. Call `details.cancel()` in the callback to keep the current value. A controller from `createSegmentedControlController()` checks an item from anywhere, like the Show Month button below. Create one controller per mounted control.
demos.caption: Choose Day, then press Show Month. The console logs each change and its reason.

demos.heading: Form
demos.intro: Each item renders a hidden native radio, so the control takes part in forms. Set `name` to submit the checked value; nothing submits without a name or a checked item. `required` blocks submission until there's a choice, `form` joins a form by its id from elsewhere on the page, and a reset returns to `defaultValue`.
demos.caption: Choose Dark and Compact, then press Save. The console logs both values, and Reset returns each control to its default.

demos.heading: Items as Data
demos.intro: The select can render bare items from this data. To style them, keep `items` on `Select` and render `SelectItem` parts inside `SelectContent`, as the example does. Keeping the data on the root also makes labels available before the list opens, including during server rendering.
demos.caption: Open Plan to see the options, separator, and Contact sales group. Education is disabled; choose Enterprise to update the value.

demos.heading: Groups
demos.intro: Put related items inside `SelectGroup` and name each group with `SelectGroupLabel`. `SelectSeparator` adds a visual break without becoming an option.
demos.caption: Open Font and choose from Sans serif, Serif or Monospace. Each group has a label that screen readers announce.

demos.heading: Icons
demos.intro: The full example marks directional icons with `mirror`, so they flip in right-to-left layouts. Items containing only an icon still need an `aria-label`.
demos.caption: Choose Center or End. Both the label and the icon in the trigger update to match the selected item.

demos.heading: Typeahead
demos.intro: Set an item's `label` when its content includes extra text that shouldn't be matched. Here, country names match typing; calling codes don't.
demos.caption: Focus Country and type “sw” to select Sweden without opening the list. Open it and type “g” to highlight Germany, then press Enter.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: A disabled select can't be focused or changed and doesn't submit a value. A read-only select stays focusable and submits its value, but can't change. Keyboard navigation skips disabled items, and they can't be chosen.
demos.caption: Billing country is disabled and Shipping from is read-only. Open Shipping to and press the arrow keys: the highlight skips Denmark, which can't be chosen.

demos.heading: Clear Button
demos.intro: Keep the clear button beside the trigger: a button can't contain another button. `keepMounted` lets it stay in the DOM when there is nothing to clear.
demos.caption: Press the clear button. The trigger shows Unassigned, focus returns to it, and the console logs null. Choose someone to bring the button back.

demos.heading: Multiple
demos.intro: `SelectValue` exposes the selected `labels` to its `children` snippet. Use them to summarize a long selection, as this example does.
demos.caption: Choose several languages, then choose one again to remove it. The list stays open, and the console logs the array.

demos.heading: Select All
demos.intro: `SelectValue maxLabels={2}` shows up to two labels and summarizes the remaining values. `getMoreLabel` lets you write that summary.
demos.caption: Open Regions and press Select all. Press it again to clear the selection, then choose one region to see the mixed state.

demos.heading: Search with Groups
demos.intro: Groups with no matching items hide automatically. `SelectItemText` can highlight the matching text; this example reads `state.segments` in its `render` snippet to bold the matches. Closing the popup clears the search.
demos.caption: Open Country and type “ja”. Only Asia Pacific and Japan remain. Try “zz” to see the empty message, then clear the search to show every country.

demos.heading: Async Search
demos.intro: This example uses Async Options to replace stale requests and load another page through `onLoadMore`. `SelectStatus` shows loading and result counts. Without a status part, Select announces result counts through the page's live region.
demos.caption: Open Country and type “an”. Results arrive after a short delay. Clear the search and move or scroll to the last result to load another page.

demos.heading: Object Values
demos.intro: A value can be an object. Tell Select how to identify it, display it, and compare it with another copy:
demos.caption: Inès starts selected even though the initial value is a copy of her item. Choose another assignee; the console logs the ID the form submits.

demos.heading: Virtualized
demos.intro: The example includes its own small row-windowing helpers. You can use the same props with a virtualizer of your choice.
demos.caption: Open Item and press End to reach Item 10000, then Home to return to the beginning. Scroll through the list; only nearby rows render.

demos.heading: Align Item with Trigger
demos.intro: Set `alignItemWithTrigger` on `SelectContent` to place the selected item over the trigger. It falls back to normal popup placement when opened by touch or when there isn't enough room.
demos.caption: Open Priority: Medium sits over the trigger. Close it, uncheck Align item with trigger, and open it again to compare placement.

demos.heading: Scrollable
demos.intro: Limit the content's height and allow vertical scrolling. `--available-height` tells you how much room the popup has; the highlighted item scrolls into view as you move with the keyboard.
demos.caption: Open Time zone and move down with the arrow keys. The list scrolls to keep the highlighted option visible.

demos.heading: Invalid
demos.intro: Inside a Field, the field's label names the trigger, its description and errors describe it, and its `name` is used for submission. After invalid submission, the trigger gets `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid`.
demos.caption: Press Continue without choosing a shipping method to show the error. Choose one and continue; the console logs the submitted value.

demos.heading: Forms
demos.intro: The example also uses `autoComplete="country"` for autofill and `form="select-newsletter"` to associate the Frequency select with a form it sits outside.
demos.caption: Choose a country and some topics, change Frequency, then press Save; the console logs all three fields. Reset restores the initial choices.

demos.heading: Presentation
demos.intro: The content gets `data-presentation`, and its render state includes `presentation`. Use either to give sheet items more space. Keep the sheet's `translate` property free for its drag behavior, and include safe-area padding at the bottom.
demos.caption: Open Status to show the bottom sheet. Choose an option to close it, or drag down to dismiss it without changing the value.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a separator between groups of content that a reader should take as separate, like a profile's header and its bio.
demos.caption: Read the profile with a screen reader. It announces a separator between Hollis Grant's name and email and the bio below.

demos.heading: Vertical
demos.intro: Set `orientation="vertical"` for a line between items in a row. It takes the row's height.
demos.caption: Read across Privacy, Terms and Cookies. A screen reader announces a vertical separator between each link.

demos.heading: Stacked Content
demos.intro: A vertical separator stretches to the tallest item in its row, so it spans a number and its label.
demos.caption: Compare the lines with the stats. Each one runs the full height of Projects, Followers and Following.

demos.heading: Rows
demos.intro: Put a separator between each pair of rows to divide a list of details.
demos.caption: Read the plan details with a screen reader. It announces a separator between Plan, Seats and Renews.

demos.heading: Decorative
demos.intro: Set `decorative` when the line adds no information. Here, the word “or” already says the two ways to sign in are separate, so a screen reader skips the lines.
demos.caption: Read from Sign In with Passkey to Email Me a Link with a screen reader. It reads “or” and skips the lines.

demos.heading: Range
demos.intro: Pass an array for a range, then render one thumb per number. Give each thumb its `index`, from 0, and its own name, like "Minimum price". The indicator fills the space between the first and the last thumb, and the `FieldLabel` names the group.
demos.caption: Move either end of Price. The thumbs stay in order.

demos.heading: Multiple Thumbs
demos.intro: Any number of thumbs works the same way. They never pass each other, and a press on the track moves the nearest one.
demos.caption: Adjust Low, Medium and High independently, without moving one past another.

demos.heading: Vertical
demos.intro: Set `orientation="vertical"` and give the slider a height. The bottom is the minimum, ArrowUp increases the value, and every part gets `data-orientation`, so `[data-orientation="vertical"]` styles the vertical axis.
demos.caption: Drag up or down, or use the arrow keys, to adjust Bass and Treble.

demos.heading: Field
demos.intro: Put the slider in a `Field`. The label names the thumb, the description describes it, and `SliderValue` shows the value beside the label. Screen readers don't announce `SliderValue` as it changes, since the thumb already says its value.
demos.caption: Click the Volume label to focus the thumb, then use the arrow keys to change the value.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Set `disabled`. A disabled slider can't be focused or moved, and isn't submitted. A disabled `<fieldset>` around it disables it too.
demos.caption: Brightness keeps its value, but can't be focused or dragged.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind `bind:value`, or pass `value` and handle `onValueChange`, to control the slider. The value keeps its shape: a number stays a number and an array stays an array. Every change carries a reason, like `drag`, `track-press` or `step-key`, and `details.thumb` says which thumb moved. Call `details.cancel()` to keep the current value.
demos.caption: Drag either Temperature thumb to log the range and its reason. Reset sets the value from outside.

demos.heading: Step and Bounds
demos.intro: `min` and `max` set the bounds, 0 and 100 by default, and `step` sets how far one step moves, counted from `min`. Decimal steps avoid floating-point drift, so a 0.1 step can reach 0.3 cleanly. When the steps from `min` don't land on `max`, the highest step below it is the end.
demos.caption: Move Year in steps of five, and Opacity in steps of 0.05.

demos.heading: Large Step
demos.intro: Arrow keys move one step. Page Up, Page Down and Shift with an arrow key move by `largeStep`, which is ten steps unless you set it. Home and End go to the bounds.
demos.caption: Focus Zoom and press an arrow key to move 1%, then Page Up, Page Down or Shift with an arrow key to move 25%.

demos.heading: Distance Between Thumbs
demos.intro: Set `minStepsBetweenThumbs` to keep neighbouring thumbs that many steps apart. A thumb stops at its neighbour, and Home and End move it only as far as its neighbour allows.
demos.caption: Move either end of Opening hours. The thumbs stay at least four hours apart.

demos.heading: Format and Locale
demos.intro: `format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` options, like `{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }` or `{ style: "percent" }`, or a function of the value. It sets what `SliderValue` shows and what screen readers announce for each thumb, while the value stays a plain number. `locale` sets separators, digits and symbol placement. Without it, the slider uses the page's `lang`, or the browser's language, once the page is interactive. Server markup uses English until then, so it never disagrees with the client.
demos.caption: Adjust Budget, Opacity, Weight, Duration and Preis to compare currency, a percentage, a unit, a custom function and German formatting.

demos.heading: Saving on Commit
demos.intro: `onValueChange` runs on every step of a drag. `onValueCommit` runs once, when the interaction that changed the value ends: the pointer lifts, the key comes up, or a screen reader adjusts it. Use the commit callback to save once per interaction. A press that doesn't change the value commits nothing.
demos.caption: Drag Brightness and release it, or press an arrow key. The console logs the value once, when you let go.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: A controller, from `createSliderController()`, moves the slider from anywhere with `setValue()`, reads it with `getValue()` and focuses a thumb with `focus()`. Values set through it are clamped, snapped to the step and sorted, and reported with the `imperative` reason.
demos.caption: Use Mute, Louder and Focus to operate Volume from outside the slider. The console logs each change with the imperative reason, and Read logs the value.

demos.heading: Form
demos.intro: `required` adds `data-required`. A slider always has a value, so it never blocks a form.
demos.caption: Adjust the filters and press Save to log the submitted values. Distance sits outside the form and joins it by id. Reset restores the defaults.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Every part takes a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state, and the `children` snippet receives the state too, like whether a thumb is being dragged, its `thumbValue` and its `percent` along the track. Here the thumb renders a `span`, its `children` add a bubble with its value, and `SliderValue`'s `children` add a percent sign.
demos.caption: Focus or drag the Brightness thumb to show its value above it.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a switch for a setting that takes effect as soon as it changes, like Airplane mode or a notification preference. Keep its label the same in both states: the label says what the setting is, and the switch shows whether it's on.
demos.caption: Click Airplane mode, or focus the switch and press Space, to turn it on and off.

demos.heading: Description
demos.intro: Use `FieldLabel` and `FieldDescription` when a setting needs more explanation. The field connects both to the switch.
demos.caption: Click Weekly digest. The field connects the label and description to the switch.

demos.heading: Choice Card
demos.intro: A setting can fill a whole card. Here the label's `::after` covers the card, so a click anywhere on it toggles the switch, and `:has([data-checked])` marks the cards that are on.
demos.caption: Click anywhere on the Public profile card to turn it on. Each card's switch keeps its own value.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: `disabled` prevents focus and changes, and leaves the switch out of form submissions. A disabled `fieldset` does the same.
demos.caption: Security alerts are always on, so that switch is disabled. Clicking it leaves it on, and Tab skips it.

demos.heading: Read-Only
demos.intro: `readOnly` keeps the switch focusable and included in form submissions, while preventing the user from changing it. Use it for a setting managed somewhere else.
demos.caption: Tab to Encrypt backups. Space and clicks leave it on.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind `bind:checked`, or pass `checked` and handle `onCheckedChange`, to own the value. A controller from `createSwitchController()` changes it from anywhere, like the Toggle button below. See State and Events for the shared change callback.
demos.caption: Turn Wi-Fi off, or press Toggle. The console logs each change and its reason.

demos.heading: Form
demos.intro: Set `name` to include the switch in a native form. A switch that's on submits its `value`, which defaults to `"on"`; a switch that's off submits nothing. Reset returns it to `defaultChecked`. Set `form` to a form's id to join it from elsewhere on the page.
demos.caption: Turn on Product updates and press Save. The console logs the submitted values, and Reset restores the defaults.

demos.heading: Validation
demos.intro: `required` blocks submission until the switch is on. In a Field, `FieldError` shows the message under the switch and connects it to the switch. Forms and Validation covers the shared field behavior.
demos.caption: Press Continue with the switch off to see the error. Turn on Two-factor authentication and continue; the console logs the submitted value.

demos.heading: Saving on Toggle
demos.intro: The example ignores presses while a save is running, and shows a spinner in the thumb. `aria-busy` tells assistive technology the switch is busy; the callback is what blocks another change.
demos.caption: Turn on Automatic backups. The thumb shows a spinner while it saves, then the switch turns on.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: The switch and thumb take a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state. Keep the part's props on the element so its role, label and keyboard behavior stay connected. See Parts and Composition for the rendering contract.
demos.caption: Turn on Dark mode. The thumb renders a sun or a moon from its state.

demos.heading: Vertical
demos.intro: Set `orientation="vertical"` to use Up and Down Arrow instead. Style the list as a column beside the panels to match.
demos.caption: Focus General, then press Down Arrow to choose Security. Up Arrow moves back through the vertical list.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Add `disabled` to a tab to prevent selection. Arrow keys can still focus it so people can discover it.
demos.caption: Use the arrow keys to reach Reports. It can receive focus, but pressing it leaves the current panel selected.

demos.heading: Icons
demos.intro: Put decorative icons in `TabsTabIcon` so they stay out of the tab’s accessible name. Add `mirror` to directional icons, such as Reply, to flip them in right-to-left text. An icon-only tab still needs an `aria-label`.
demos.caption: Choose Replies. Its directional icon mirrors when the surrounding page uses right-to-left text.

demos.heading: Manual Activation
demos.intro: A panel becomes a tab stop only when it has no focusable content. A panel with a field lets Tab go straight to the field.
demos.caption: Focus Preview, then press Right Arrow. Code receives focus; press Enter or Space to show its panel. Tab then moves into the Source field.

demos.heading: Loop
demos.intro: Arrow keys normally wrap around at either end. Set `loop={false}` to stop there instead.
demos.caption: Focus Year and press Right Arrow. Focus stays at the end because looping is off.

demos.heading: Indicator
demos.intro: Add transitions for the properties you animate. Skip them while `data-activation-direction="none"` to avoid animating the first placement.
demos.caption: Choose Podcasts, then choose Vertical. The same indicator measures and follows the selected tab in either layout.

demos.heading: Keep Mounted
demos.intro: Panels normally unmount when another tab is selected. Add `keepMounted` to a panel to keep its content hidden in the page, preserving local state such as a draft.
demos.caption: Write a message, switch to Formatting, then return to Reply. Your draft is still there.

demos.heading: Find in Page
demos.intro: Server-rendered panels retain `hidden="until-found"`, so their content is available to Find before hydration.
demos.caption: Use your browser’s Find command to search for “restocking fee”. Returns opens to reveal the match.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: Use `data-activation-direction` to choose a slide direction. Put the panels in the same grid cell so they overlap during the transition, as this example does.
demos.caption: Move between Overview, Activity and Settings. The panels slide in the direction you moved.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: `onValueChange` receives the new value and a reason, such as `item-press`, `list-navigation`, or `imperative`. It does not run for the initial selection. A controller lets another control select a tab too.
demos.caption: Choose Drafts, then press Show Sent Mail. The console logs each new value with its reason.

demos.heading: Links
demos.intro: Render a tab as a link when selection should navigate. It keeps its tab role; arrow keys follow the link when they select it. Modified clicks, such as Cmd-click, keep their normal browser behavior without selecting the tab.
demos.caption: Choose Activity. Its panel opens and the URL hash changes. Modified clicks keep the link’s usual browser behavior.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Use the `render` snippet to change a part’s element or add to its content, as in the links example. Parts and Composition covers the shared rendering API. Each part’s state is listed under State.
demos.caption: Each tab renders its own button with an unread count after the label. Choose Unread to see who wrote to you.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A textarea is a native multi-line text field for messages, notes and descriptions. It works inside a field and a form, can grow with its text, and reports the same change reasons as Input.
demos.caption: Click Message to focus the textarea, then type. Press Enter to start a new line.

demos.heading: Field
demos.intro: Wrap the textarea in a Field to give it a visible label and a description. The field also supplies its `name` when the textarea has none.
demos.caption: Click Feedback to focus the textarea. A screen reader reads the description with the field.

demos.heading: Auto Resize
demos.intro: Set `autoResize` to grow and shrink the textarea with its text. CSS `min-height` and `max-height` set its limits; past the maximum, the text scrolls inside it.
demos.caption: Type several lines in Notes. The textarea grows with each line until it reaches its maximum height, then scrolls. Delete the lines and it shrinks back.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind the value with `bind:value`, or pass `value` and handle `onValueChange`. Here the character count is derived from that value, and the native `maxlength` caps the text.
demos.caption: Edit Bio and watch the character count under it. The textarea stops accepting text at 160 characters.

demos.heading: Form
demos.intro: A textarea submits its value through a native form under its field's `name`. Pass a controller from `createInputController()` to change it from outside, here to empty it after sending. The native `required` constraint blocks an empty message.
demos.caption: Type a message and press Send Message. The console logs it and the textarea clears. Pressing Send Message while it's empty is blocked.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Set `disabled` on the textarea or its field to prevent editing and leave it out of the tab order and the submitted values.
demos.caption: Try to edit Reply or reach it with Tab. The disabled textarea keeps its value but can't be changed.

demos.heading: Invalid
demos.intro: Set `invalid` on the field for an error your app decides. The field shows its error, associates it with the textarea and sets `aria-invalid`. Field covers native constraints and error matches.
demos.caption: Focus Review. The textarea is marked invalid, and the error below says how long the review should be.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Time Input for a time of day, like a meeting or an opening hour. It works like Date Input, with segments for the hour, the minute and, on a 12-hour clock, AM or PM.
demos.caption: Click the hour and type 230, then P. Press ArrowUp or ArrowDown on a part to step it.

demos.heading: Clock and Seconds
demos.intro: The input shows the locale's clock. Set `hourCycle` to `12` or `24` to choose one, and `granularity` to `"second"` to add seconds, or `"hour"` to show the hour alone.
demos.caption: The same evening time on a 12-hour clock, a 24-hour clock and with seconds. All three submit 24-hour values.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Timeline for a list of things that happened, or will: a project's activity, an order's status history, a release's milestones. It's a list for screen readers, with one tab stop for keyboards, and the arrow keys move between events.
demos.caption: Tab into the activity, then use Up and Down to move between events. Home and End jump to the first and last.

demos.heading: Horizontal
demos.intro: Set `orientation="horizontal"` for a row, like a roadmap. Left and Right move between events instead of Up and Down, and they swap in right-to-left text. Set `loop={false}` to stop at either end.
demos.caption: Tab into the roadmap and press Right to reach Launch. Right again stays there.

demos.heading: Status
demos.intro: Create a controller with `createTimelineController` and call its `focus()` with an item's `value` to move focus to it from anywhere.
demos.caption: Tab into the order status. Focus starts on Shipped, the current step. Move away, then choose Go to Current Step.

demos.heading: Details
demos.intro: Put a Collapsible inside an item for details that can open. Its trigger is a button inside the event, so Tab reaches it after the event, and arrow keys still move between events.
demos.caption: Tab to What Changed under Version 2.4 and press Enter. Shift+Tab back to the event, then press Down for Version 2.3.

demos.heading: Feed
demos.intro: Set `busy` while you load or change articles. It sets `aria-busy`, so screen readers wait for the new articles before reading on.
demos.caption: Tab into the updates and press Page Down. Choose Load More: the feed is busy until three more updates arrive. The console logs each load.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A toast tells someone that something happened, like a saved change or a sent message, and goes away on its own. It can offer an action such as Undo, stacks with the toasts before it, and is announced to screen readers without taking focus.
demos.caption: Press Create Event. Choose Undo, swipe the toast away, or wait for it to close. Undo logs Event removed.

demos.heading: Types
demos.intro: `toast.success`, `.info`, `.warning`, `.error` and `.loading` set the toast's type, which the toast exposes as `data-type` for an icon or a color. Errors are announced right away and other types wait for a pause; set `priority` to change that. A loading toast stays until it's updated or dismissed.
demos.caption: Choose a type. Each toast shows its type's icon, and Loading turns into Photos uploaded when it finishes.

demos.heading: Position
demos.intro: Set the region's `side` to `top` or `bottom`, and `align` to `start`, `center` or `end`. Start and end follow the writing direction. A toast can be swiped toward the side and, unless it's centered, toward the end it's aligned to.
demos.caption: Choose a side and an alignment, then press Create Event and look for the toast at that edge of the page.

demos.heading: Action and Cancel
demos.intro: Add an `action`, like Undo, and a `cancel` button that dismisses the toast. Their callbacks can update your app. `onDismiss` tells you why the toast is closing, and `details.cancel()` keeps it open; a canceled timeout starts the countdown again.
demos.caption: Press Archive Message, then choose Undo or Dismiss, swipe the toast away, or let it time out. The console logs why it closed.

demos.heading: Link
demos.intro: Give an action an `href` to render it as a link. It keeps normal link behavior, including opening in a new tab.
demos.caption: Press Send Invoice, then follow View in the toast.

demos.heading: Promise
demos.intro: `toast.promise()` shows a loading toast, then updates the same toast when the promise resolves or rejects. Each message can be a string, options with a description or an action, or a function of the result. A toast dismissed while loading stays closed.
demos.caption: Press Save Changes to see Saving changes become Changes saved. Press it again for the error, then choose Retry.

demos.heading: Stacking
demos.intro: `maxVisible` limits how many toasts show at once, three by default; the rest wait in the queue, and their timers start when they show. The stack expands while the pointer or focus is in it. Set `expanded` to keep it open. Styling shows the CSS that lays out the stack.
demos.caption: Press Add Toast a few times, then hover the stack to expand it. Past four toasts, the rest wait their turn. Check Always expanded to keep it open.

demos.heading: Duration
demos.intro: Set `duration` in milliseconds, on the toaster or on one toast, or `Infinity` for a toast that stays until it's dismissed. The default is five seconds. Timers pause while the pointer or focus is in the region, and while the page is hidden or its window is inactive.
demos.caption: Press each button. Hover a toast to pause its timer. The session toast stays until you press Got It.

demos.heading: Update and Dismiss
demos.intro: Keep the id `toast()` returns to update or dismiss that toast, or pass your own `id`. `toast.update()` returns whether the toast was still there, and `toast.dismiss()` without an id closes every toast.
demos.caption: Press Upload Report and watch one toast count up to Report uploaded. Cancel Upload closes it early, and Dismiss All clears every toast.

demos.heading: Async Action
demos.intro: Return a promise from an action to keep the toast open while it runs. The action's state has `pending` while it runs and `error` if it fails, so the button can say Restoring… or offer a retry, and presses are ignored until it settles. See Button for changes made after an `await`.
demos.caption: Press Delete File, then Undo. The button shows Restoring… until the restore finishes, then the toast closes.

demos.heading: Keyboard Shortcut
demos.intro: F6 moves focus to the newest toast and back. Set the region's `shortcut` to use another key, or `null` to turn it off. The region advertises it through `aria-keyshortcuts`.
demos.caption: Press Send Message, then Alt+T (Option+T on a Mac) to focus the toast. Press Escape to dismiss it, or Alt+T again to go back.

demos.heading: Overlay Host and Confirm
demos.intro: To style the question, render an `AlertDialog` with the confirm controller and read the question from its content's `payload`. Alert Dialog covers `createConfirm()` in more detail.
demos.caption: Press Delete on a project and confirm. The row goes away and a toast says so. Reset Projects brings them back.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Pass anything else your toast needs in `data`, and read it from the toast the region's `children` snippet receives. Every part also takes a `render` snippet; this example renders each toast's `li` itself, making the ones hidden behind a collapsed stack `inert`.
demos.caption: Press New Message to show a toast with Hollis Grant's initials. Choose Reply or close it.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a toggle for a button that stays on until you press it again, like starring a document or turning on Bold. Put several in a toggle group to share one value, as a text editor's formatting buttons or a view switcher do.
demos.caption: Press the star beside Q3 Roadmap, or focus it and press Enter or Space. It fills in while pressed, and its accessible name stays Star.

demos.heading: Group
demos.intro: Put toggles in a `ToggleGroup`, from the same `@ui-sdk/svelte/toggle` entry, to share a value and arrow-key navigation. Give the group an accessible name and each toggle a `value`. Set `multiple` to let several toggles stay pressed.
demos.caption: Press Bold and Italic to keep both pressed. Left and Right move focus without changing either.

demos.heading: Single Selection
demos.intro: Without `multiple`, pressing a toggle unpresses the others. Pressing the pressed toggle again clears the selection, unless you set `deselectable` to `false`, as this alignment group does. `deselectable` doesn't choose an initial value for you, so pair it with `defaultValue`.
demos.caption: Press Align center to replace Align start, then press Align center again. One alignment always stays pressed.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Every part takes a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state. A toggle's state has `pressed`, and a group's has `value`, its pressed values. Keep the part's props on the button, so its `aria-pressed` and keyboard behavior stay connected. See Parts and Composition for the rendering contract.
