demos.caption: Press Favorite. The heart renders filled or empty from the toggle's pressed state.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A token input is a text field that holds tokens alongside the text, like the people mentioned in a message or the files attached to a prompt. Each token moves, deletes and copies as one piece.
demos.caption: Type @ and choose a person with the arrow keys and Enter. Remove a token with Backspace, or press its remove button.

demos.heading: Prompt Input
demos.intro: Combine file suggestions, skills, and a send action. This example marks files as pending while they load, then uses `updateToken()` to show a skill running. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line. An open suggestion menu or an active input method takes precedence over sending.
demos.caption: Type @ for files or / at the start for skills. For /search, enter a query and press Enter to insert the command. Press Enter again to send, and the console logs the message.

demos.heading: Deleting Tokens
demos.intro: Choose what Backspace does at a token with `tokenDeletion`:
demos.caption: Choose a Backspace behavior, click just after routes.ts, and press Backspace. Undo to try another behavior.

demos.heading: Codec
demos.intro: Use `toText`, `fromText`, and `toLabel` to convert values yourself. Supply a custom codec for another format, as this example does for `<@hollis>`. With `copy="label"`, copying writes what people read, and pasting back into a token input still restores the tokens. The default parser accepts letters, digits, `_`, and `-` in token types; other types need a custom codec.
demos.caption: Edit the message. The console logs it in the custom format, with each mention as <@id>.

demos.heading: Form
demos.intro: Give the input a `name` to submit its serialized text. `required`, `disabled`, and `readOnly` control form behavior. The `form` option associates it with a form elsewhere on the page, as shown here.
demos.caption: Press Submit to log the prompt's serialized value. Try Disabled and Read-only, then Reset.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind `bind:value`, or pass `value` and update it in `onValueChange`. The change details include the reason, input type, and removed tokens. The input still manages its editing history.
demos.caption: Type, add a file with @, or remove a token. The console logs the value and the reason for each change.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: Use `createTokenInputController()` to insert, update, or remove tokens from code. Pass a promise as `resolve` to mark an inserted token as pending until its data is ready. Updating a token doesn't add an undo step.
demos.caption: Attach a file and watch it load. Show the first token's full path or remove it, then use Undo or Clear.

demos.heading: Submit Shortcut
demos.intro: Set `submitShortcut` to `mod+enter` for a multiline message. Enter then inserts a line, and Command or Control+Enter submits.
demos.caption: Write a message. Enter adds a line; Command+Enter on a Mac or Control+Enter elsewhere sends it to the console.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Toolbar to group the controls of an editor, a canvas or a table. Tab enters it once, and the arrow keys move between its buttons, toggles, menus and fields.
demos.caption: Tab into the toolbar, then use Left and Right to move between Bold, Italic, Underline and Insert link. Press Space to toggle the focused style. The console logs each change.

demos.heading: Toggle Groups
demos.intro: A Toggle group inside a toolbar joins its navigation instead of adding another tab stop. Arrow keys move focus without pressing anything; Enter or Space presses the focused toggle.
demos.caption: Arrow from the alignment group to the list group, then press Space on Align center or Numbered list. The console logs each choice.

demos.heading: Groups
demos.intro: Use `ToolbarGroup` to name related controls. Set `disabled` on the group to disable them together; they stay focusable with `aria-disabled`.
demos.caption: Move through Cut, Copy and Paste into History with the arrow keys. Undo and Redo stay focusable but do nothing.

demos.heading: Menus
demos.intro: Render a Menu trigger through `ToolbarButton`. In a horizontal toolbar, Down opens the menu while Left and Right keep moving between toolbar items.
demos.caption: Focus Share and press Down, then choose Email or Copy Link. Escape closes the menu and returns focus to Share.

demos.heading: Selects
demos.intro: A Select trigger joins the same way. It keeps its select behavior while it takes part in the toolbar's focus order.
demos.caption: Open Zoom and choose a value, or step it with Zoom out and Zoom in. Each button turns off at the end of the range.

demos.heading: Fields
demos.intro: Entering a field with an arrow puts its caret at the far end in that direction: press the same arrow again to leave, or the other arrow to edit. A number input keeps Up and Down for stepping its value.
demos.caption: Move into Font size and press Up or Down to change it. In Find, type a word, then move the caret to an edge before that arrow leaves the field.

demos.heading: Links
demos.intro: `ToolbarLink` joins the same focus order and keeps its link behavior. The demo handles a plain click itself and leaves modified clicks, like opening in a new tab, to the browser.
demos.caption: Arrow to Files Changed and press Enter. The console logs the page it opened.

demos.heading: Vertical
demos.intro: Set `orientation="vertical"` to move with Up and Down, like a canvas tool palette. Separators turn to run across the toolbar.
demos.caption: Use Up and Down to move between the tools and Delete. Space picks the focused tool.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: A disabled item stays reachable with `aria-disabled`, so people can find it, but it ignores presses, including keys meant for a component rendered through it. Set `focusableWhenDisabled` to `false` to skip it instead.
demos.caption: Arrow from Reply to Archive, which is disabled but focusable. Delete is skipped. Only Reply logs a press.

demos.heading: Loop
demos.intro: Arrow keys wrap from the last item to the first by default. Set `loop` to `false` to stop at the ends.
demos.caption: Focus Last and press Right. Focus stays there; Home still moves to First.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: Create a controller with `createToolbarController` and pass it as `controller`. Its `focus()` moves focus to the item focused last, like the Alt+F10 shortcut editors give their toolbars. Create one controller per toolbar.
demos.caption: Type in Notes, then press Alt+F10 or choose Focus Toolbar. Press a toolbar button and the console logs it.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A tooltip names a control or adds a short hint when the pointer rests on it or keyboard focus reaches it. Keep it to a few words of plain text.
demos.caption: The tooltip starts open. Hover the button or reach it with Tab to show it again, and Escape closes it while focus stays on the button.

demos.heading: Side
demos.intro: `side` picks where the tooltip opens: `top` by default. It flips to the other side when there isn't room, and shifts along the trigger to stay on screen. `data-side` says where it landed.
demos.caption: Hover Top, Left, Right and Bottom. Each tooltip opens on that side of its button, or flips into the middle when there isn't room.

demos.heading: Anchor
demos.intro: Position the tooltip against something other than the trigger with `anchor`: an element, a CSS selector, a point like `{ x, y }`, or anything with `getBoundingClientRect()`. Here a small help button inside a field shows its tooltip along the whole field.
demos.caption: Hover the help button. The tooltip opens below the Webhook URL field and lines up with its start, not with the button.

demos.heading: Keyboard Shortcut
demos.intro: The tooltip doesn't bind the keys. Register the shortcut yourself with `registerShortcut`, as the example does, or use the `shortcut` of a component that binds keys, like a Dialog trigger.
demos.caption: Hover Save or Share to read its shortcut, then press the button or the keys. The console logs Saved or Shared.

demos.heading: Disabled Buttons
demos.intro: A natively disabled button can't receive focus, and some browsers send it no pointer events, so its tooltip never shows. When the tooltip explains why an action is unavailable, use `aria-disabled="true"` instead and ignore the button's presses yourself. The button stays in the Tab order, screen readers announce it as dimmed, and the tooltip explains what's missing. `disabled` on the tooltip turns the explanation off once the button works.
demos.caption: Hover or focus Publish to learn what's missing. Type a title, and Publish works and its tooltip goes away.

demos.heading: Touch
demos.intro: For an info button whose only job is the tip, add `toggleable`: pressing the trigger opens and closes the tooltip, with a finger, a mouse or the keyboard, and its text is announced when a press opens it. An outside press or Escape closes it too.
demos.caption: Press the info button to open the tip, including on a touch screen. Press it again or anywhere else to close it.

demos.heading: Keep Open on Press
demos.intro: Pressing the trigger closes the tooltip, so it doesn't cover what the press changed, and it stays closed until the pointer leaves. `closeOnPress={false}` keeps it open, like for a copy button whose tooltip turns into "Copied".
demos.caption: Hover the copy button and press it. The tooltip stays open and changes to Copied.

demos.heading: Truncated Text
demos.intro: To show a tooltip only when text is cut off, cancel the open in `onOpenChange` when the text fits. Compare `scrollWidth` with `clientWidth` in the callback. The tooltip repeats the name, so `type="label"` keeps screen readers from hearing it twice.
demos.caption: Hover or focus each file. Only names that are cut off open a tooltip.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind `open` with `bind:open`, and read each change in `onOpenChange`. Every change carries a reason, like `trigger-hover`, `trigger-focus`, `trigger-press`, `escape-key` or `outside-press`. Call `details.cancel()` to stop it. To open the tooltip from anywhere, like a step in a guided tour, use a controller.
demos.caption: Check Open, or hover Export. The console logs each change and its reason.

demos.heading: Shared
demos.intro: Only the trigger that opened the tooltip is described by it, so give each trigger a name of its own, like an `aria-label`. The controller's `open()` takes a payload and an `anchor` too, and on an open tooltip, `open({ payload })` replaces the payload, like another trigger taking it over. `onPayloadChange` reports each change.
demos.caption: Move along Bold, Italic and Underline. One tooltip follows the pointer and shows each button's label.

demos.heading: Animation
demos.intro: For people who ask for less motion, drop the scale in a `prefers-reduced-motion` query and keep the fade. `onOpenChangeComplete` runs once the tooltip has finished opening or closing, after any animation, with the new open state.
demos.caption: Hover Archive, then move away. The tooltip grows out of the button and fades, and the console logs Opening, Open, Closing and Closed.

demos.heading: Custom Rendering
demos.intro: Every part takes a `render` snippet, which receives the props to spread and the part's state. See Parts and Composition for prop merging and state-based rendering.
demos.caption: Hover Changelog. The trigger renders as a link, and its tooltip says where it goes.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Tree when items have children, like files in folders or pages in a docs sidebar. Start with nested parts, then add selection, checkboxes, or children loaded from a server as you need them.
demos.caption: Expand components to see its files. Use the arrow keys to move between rows and open or close branches.

demos.heading: File Paths
demos.intro: Selection and activation are separate. This example uses `activation="automatic"` so arrow keys select a file, then `onAction` opens it. Return a promise from the action callback to show a pending state while it opens.
demos.caption: Arrow down to package.json, then press Enter. It shows a spinner while it opens, then the console logs Opened package.json.

demos.heading: Multiple Selection
demos.intro: `mode="multiple"` makes the value an array. Cmd-click or Ctrl-click toggles one item, Shift extends a range, and Cmd+A or Ctrl+A selects the visible items. This example sets `expandOnPress` to `false`, so clicking Inbox or Projects selects the folder without closing it.
demos.caption: Cmd-click or Ctrl-click Archive to add it to the selection. Shift-click or Shift+Arrow extends a range, and the console logs what's selected.

demos.heading: Checkboxes
demos.intro: `checkStrategy` chooses what the `checked` array reports:
demos.caption: Press Space on Vue, then on Frontend. Frontend is mixed while only some of its items are checked, and the console logs the trunk strategy's values.

demos.heading: Links
demos.intro: Set `mode="none"` for a navigation tree, then render labels as links. `current` identifies the current page with `aria-current="page"`, expands its ancestors, and gives it the initial Tab stop. Update it when your route changes.
demos.caption: Choose Dialog. The current-page marker moves to it, and you stay on this docs page.

demos.heading: Disabled
demos.intro: Disabled items can't be selected, checked, expanded, or run. They stay focusable so screen readers can find them. Set `focusableWhenDisabled` to `false` to skip them, or `disabled` on the root to disable the whole tree. A disabled `<fieldset>` around the tree disables it too.
demos.caption: Arrow through Enterprise while Focusable when disabled is on. Turn it off and the same arrow keys skip disabled items.

demos.heading: Loading Children
demos.intro: Use the supplied `signal` to cancel a request. Trying to expand the branch again while it loads aborts it. A rejection sets `data-failed`, and the next attempt retries. `announcement` lets you customize loading and failure messages.
demos.caption: Expand users to load its files. Archive fails on its first attempt and shows a retry icon; expand it again to load it.

demos.heading: Virtualized
demos.intro: `onHighlight` reports the focused item's index among visible rows. Use it to scroll before mounting a row that is outside the rendered range. Every item sets `--tree-level`, so the stylesheet indents the flat rows by their level.
demos.caption: Expand folders or press End to focus Folder 100. The tree has 10,100 items, but only nearby rows render.

demos.heading: Find in Page
demos.intro: `hiddenUntilFound` keeps collapsed groups in the DOM with `hidden="until-found"`. In browsers that support it, Find in Page can match a hidden item and open its ancestors. Use `keepMounted` when you only need collapsed content to stay mounted, without browser search.
demos.caption: Use your browser's Find command to look for Phobos, a moon of Mars. The matching branches open to reveal it.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: A `createTreeController()` instance can expand or collapse branches, change selection and checkboxes, or focus an item. `reveal(value)` opens an item's ancestors, scrolls it into view, and focuses it. Supply the hierarchy through `items`, as this example does, or keep collapsed groups mounted so their descendants are known. See Controllers for setup and lifecycle.
demos.caption: Press Find Two-Factor to open Account and Security, then select and focus Two-factor authentication. Collapse All closes every branch.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: A trigger menu suggests what to insert when someone types a trigger character, like `@` for people or `/` for commands. It opens at the caret, narrows as they type, and inserts the choice into the text.
demos.caption: Type @, narrow the list with a name, and press Enter to insert the highlighted person.

demos.heading: Triggers as Data
demos.intro: Give each trigger a `char` and its `items`. Items can be strings, objects, groups or a loader, and they render themselves when you leave out `TriggerMenuContent`. The same field can offer people after `@`, commands after `/` and channels after `#`.
demos.caption: Type @ for people, / at the start for commands, or # to load channels.

demos.heading: Commands with Arguments
demos.intro: A trigger with `boundary: "start"` matches only at the start of the text, so a leading space escapes it. An item with `arguments` asks for each one in order: `TriggerMenuHint` shows what's left at the caret, Tab accepts the highlighted suggestion and moves to the next argument, Enter finishes once only optional arguments remain, and Backspace past an argument's start goes back. An argument without `items` is free text. `after: "submit"` sends the form once the item is inserted.
demos.caption: Type /status, then press Tab to choose a status and an optional time, and Enter to finish. Choose /away to send it at once. The console logs each command.

demos.heading: Icons
demos.intro: Put an item's icon in a `TriggerMenuItemIcon`, before its text. Screen readers skip it, and filtering and the text a choice inserts ignore it, so an SVG's `<title>`, an icon font's glyph or an emoji never joins the item's name or the field. Items as data have no icon, so compose the items that show one.
demos.caption: Type / to open the commands, then type re to narrow them. Each icon sits before its name, and filtering ignores it.

demos.heading: Loading Items
demos.intro: A trigger's `items` can be a loader, called with the query and an `AbortSignal` once typing pauses. A newer query aborts the older load, so only its results land, and the last results stay while the next ones load. `TriggerMenuStatus` and `TriggerMenuEmpty` get `loading`, and while a load runs, `aria-busy` marks the list, so you can fade the results that are about to change.
demos.caption: Type # and a channel name. The list says it's loading, and older results fade while newer ones load.

demos.heading: Custom Items
demos.intro: Compose `TriggerMenuItem`s with any content, in groups. `label` is what's matched and inserted, `keywords` adds words to match, and `disabled` keeps an item in the list without letting it be chosen. A trigger's `spaces`, `pattern` and `maxLength` decide what its query may hold, `filter` how it narrows the items, and `insert` what replaces the trigger and query. An item's own `onSelect` runs first and can insert something else with `details.insert()`.
demos.caption: Type @ and the start of a first name to insert it, or choose Notify everyone here to insert @here. Deactivated people can't be chosen.

demos.heading: Input
demos.intro: Render the input part as an `<input>` for a single line. It's a combobox with `aria-expanded`. In a single line, Enter often submits a form, so this example sets `autoHighlight={false}`: Enter chooses only once an arrow key has highlighted a person, and `loop={false}` stops the arrows at either end of the list.
demos.caption: Type @ in the empty task. Nothing is highlighted until you press ArrowDown, then Enter assigns the person.

demos.heading: Positioning
demos.intro: By default, the list opens below the trigger at the caret and flips to stay on screen. `side`, `align` and the offsets place it, and `anchor` positions it against another element. This example opens the list above the whole field, lines its items up with the label, and renders it inside the field with `container`.
demos.caption: Type @ in the comment. The list opens above the field, lined up with its label.

demos.heading: Controlled
demos.intro: Bind `open` with `bind:open` to own the popup state, and read each change in `onOpenChange`. The details say why it changed. `onQueryChange` reports the text after the trigger and the argument being typed, and `onOpenChangeComplete` runs once the menu has finished opening or closing. Escape dismisses a match, and `shortcut` reopens it, Control+Space by default.
demos.caption: Type @ and a name, press Escape, then Control+J to reopen the list. The console logs each callback with its reason.

demos.heading: Controller
demos.intro: Create a controller with `createTriggerMenuController()` and pass it as `controller` to open suggestions, insert text at the caret, or read the current match. `open()` types the trigger at the caret and returns a Promise that resolves when the menu closes.
demos.caption: Press Mention and choose a person. The console logs why the list closed. Insert Date adds today's date at the caret.

demos.heading: Any Editor
demos.intro: Pass `editor` to connect the menu to a field you render yourself, or to another editor. `textFieldAdapter()` makes one for a textarea or an input.
demos.caption: Type @ in the notes, a textarea connected through an editor adapter, and choose a person.

demos.heading: Overview
demos.intro: Use a Waterfall for anything with a start and a duration that nests: a browser's network requests, an OpenTelemetry trace, the steps of a build. Each span is a row with its own bar, placed on one time axis, and screen reader and keyboard users get a treegrid they can walk span by span.
demos.caption: Use the arrow keys to move between requests. Press Right to move into a row's cells, where each bar reads out when its request starts and how long it takes.

demos.heading: Nested Spans
demos.intro: Clicking a row, or pressing Enter or Space on it, selects it. `bind:value` holds the selected span, like the one a details panel shows. `format` changes how times read, here as narrow milliseconds.
demos.caption: Expand payments.charge with Right, then press Enter on gateway.capture. The console logs the selected span. Collapse All closes every span.

demos.heading: Zoom
demos.intro: The `children` snippet of `WaterfallAxis` also receives its `ticks`, for ticks of your own.
demos.caption: Press Zoom In twice. The axis shows smaller steps, and the metrics span stretches past the edges.

demos.heading: Large Traces
demos.intro: `onHighlight` reports the index of the row the keyboard moves to. Scroll it into view there, so a row that isn't rendered yet takes focus once it is. An arrow key changes only the two rows it moves between, however long the trace is.
demos.caption: Press End to focus job 2000, or Page Down to move a page at a time. The trace has 10,000 spans, but only nearby rows render.
